sections.label: Surpluses and Net Investment Returns Contribution
sections.summary: Accumulated surpluses and the NIRC allow a robust response while pursuing the longer-term agenda, and without NIRC three of four fiscal years would have been in deficit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Thanks to disciplined and prudent financial management as well as the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC), the surpluses accumulated in this term of Government allow us to mount a massive and robust response to the current situation, yet allowing us to still press on with our longer-term agenda.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Without NIRC, three out of the last four fiscal years would have ended in deficit positions.

sections.label: Budget 2018 surplus and MAS contribution
sections.summary: In Budget 2018, FY2017 had a bigger than projected $10.9 billion surplus due to a one-off MAS contribution and stamp duty collections.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The calls were even louder in Budget 2018, where there was a bigger than projected surplus of $10.9 billion for financial year (FY) 2017 due to a one-off contribution from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and stamp duty collections.

sections.label: Savings for Stabilisation and Support Package
sections.summary: Savings for rainy days were used for the $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package to deal with the COVID-19 outbreak impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: A case in point here is how we used the savings for rainy days to come up with this $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package to deal with the impact from the COVID-19 outbreak.

sections.label: Job Support Scheme qualifying period
sections.summary: The qualifying period for the Job Support Scheme is salary paid during October 2019 to December 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The qualifying period for the Job Support Scheme is for salary paid during the months from October 2019 to December 2019.

sections.label: Assurance Package and GST concerns
sections.summary: The $6 billion Assurance Package helps address Singaporeans' concerns about the GST increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The $6 billion Assurance Package does help to address the concerns of Singaporeans on the GST increase.

sections.label: Assurance Package payouts and GST offsets
sections.summary: The Assurance Package, effective after the GST increase after 2021, targets lower- and middle-income households and seniors, giving adult Singaporeans $700 to $1,600 over five years and offsets covering at least five years of additional GST expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The Assurance Package that will come into effect when the GST rate increase kicks in after 2021 is specifically targeted at helping the lower- and middle-income Singaporean households and seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under the Package, every adult Singaporean will receive a cash payout of $700 to $1,600 over five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The majority of Singaporeans will receive offsets to cover at least five years' worth of additional GST expenses incurred.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In other words, to the majority of Singaporeans, the effect of the GST increase will be further pushed back by another five years when the new increase kicks in because of the Assurance Package.

sections.label: Doubling job placements for older workers
sections.summary: The Government aims to double annual job placement of local workers in their 40s and 50s to around 5,500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Under this initiative, the Government aims to double the annual job placement of local workers in their 40s and 50s to around 5,500.

sections.label: Hiring incentives for older local jobseekers
sections.summary: Employers hiring local jobseekers aged 40 and above through the reskilling programme receive 20% salary support for six months, capped at $6,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: On the other hand, we know that there are, indeed, biases on the part of employers, including ageism, when hiring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, the most significant announcement in this package is that the Government is providing hiring incentives to employers who hire local jobseekers aged 40 and above through the reskilling programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For each eligible worker, the employer will receive 20% salary support for six months, capped at $6,000.

sections.label: SkillsFuture top-up for older Singaporeans
sections.summary: The Minister announced a $500 SkillsFuture top-up for every Singaporean aged 40 to 60, giving them $1,000 SkillsFuture Credit in total.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To further encourage lifelong learning, the Minister has also announced a special SkillsFuture top-up of $500 to every Singaporean aged 40 to 60, so that this group of Singaporeans will get $1,000 SkillsFuture Credit in total.

sections.label: Landlords passing on property tax rebates
sections.summary: Landlords enjoying new 15% property tax rebates should quickly pass this on to tenants as reduced rentals or more.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, landlords who enjoy the new 15% property tax rebates should quickly pass this on to their tenants in the form of reduced rentals or do even more.

sections.label: Helping a student stay in school
sections.summary: A student was convinced to continue his studies, graduated from ITE with an award and polytechnic scholarship, and asked support be channelled to other needy families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: After he left, I asked my grassroots leader to please go and see if this is the boy that came to see me a year ago because we need to convince him that he needs to stay in school because his grades are good and we need to help his family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad to say that we were able to convince him and he did continue with his studies and we were able to help his family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: By sheer coincidence, I was invited to an ITE graduation ceremony and I witnessed the graduation of him and he was receiving an award and a scholarship to the polytechnic.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: At that time, he informed me that, with his scholarship, his family could manage and he asked that we channel the support to other more needy families.

sections.label: Budget 2020 balancing support and transformation
sections.summary: Budget 2020 provides support for workers and businesses amid COVID-19 and geopolitical tensions while staying on track with strategic economic transformation plans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: We must not, however, give up on building for the long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am glad that Budget 2020, while seeking to provide the much-needed support and help for workers and businesses to weather the short-term uncertainties brought about by the COVID-19 situation and geopolitical tensions, is also balancing this with ensuring that we stay on track with the strategic economic transformation plans to prepare Singapore and Singaporeans for the longer term and to be ready for new opportunities.

sections.label: Budget people development thrust
sections.summary: The Budget's important thrust is developing people and supporting continual learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: An important thrust of the Budget is the development of our people and supporting continual learning.

sections.label: Business transformation and job redesign measures
sections.summary: Measures encourage business transformation and job redesign, including SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit Fund control, employer-IHL partnerships, anchor enterprises, and student work experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The various measures to encourage businesses to transform their business and redesign jobs, including giving enterprises more direct control over the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit Fund of $10,000 per company, enabling partnerships among employers, institutes of higher learning (IHLs) and the involvement of large anchor enterprises to support training for their sector and value chain partners, together with providing Singaporean students real-life learning work experience.

sections.label: Asia Exposure and internship programmes
sections.summary: The Asia Exposure Programme and enhanced Global Ready Talent internships give young Singaporean students cross-cultural skills, perspectives, and regional networks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The new Asia Exposure Programme and the enhanced support for Internships under the Global Ready Talent Programme are also key platforms to give our young Singaporean students the opportunity to acquire cross-cultural skills and perspectives, developing networks of relationships and understanding of the region.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package relief
sections.summary: Short-term Stabilisation and Support Package measures give businesses COVID-19 relief and help workers retain jobs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The short-term measures in the Stabilisation and Support Package will provide businesses some relief from the impact of the COVID-19 situation and will help workers retain their jobs.

sections.label: Support for mid-career workers
sections.summary: The Budget's special focus on support for mid-career workers in their 40s and 50s is welcomed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Budget's special focus on support for mid-career workers currently in their 40s and 50s who form a significant number of the workforce is welcomed.

sections.label: PCP jobs and mid-career access
sections.summary: It asks the current number of PCP jobs in Place-and-Train or Attach-and-Train and how mid-career workers can avail themselves.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What is the current number of available jobs that the PCPs have either in the "Place-and-Train" or the "Attach-and-Train", and how can mid-career workers avail themselves of these opportunities?

sections.label: Mid-career worker employment policies
sections.summary: Employment policies and practices must align with efforts to recruit, retain and reskill mid-career Singaporeans, including onboarding and transition to new industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Another area that I would also like to highlight is as we encourage employers to recruit, retain and reskill mid-career Singaporeans, we must recognise that the current employment policies and practices need to be also aligned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: For the mid-career worker, what is additionally required is also the onboarding and transition to a new industry when you are looking at reskilling and job role changes.

sections.label: Social capability and ground-up participation
sections.summary: Performance and management systems must evolve, and Budget 2020 supports building social capability and platforms for ground-up participation and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Performance systems and management systems need to also evolve in the same way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am also encouraged that Budget 2020 focuses on supporting the building of social capability and capacity to foster a climate of change in our community and to channel the energies of our people around important social causes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Beyond the provision of funding, equally important are these platforms to encourage ground-up participation and bringing stakeholders together to catalyse more ground-up initiatives, crowd source ideas and drive innovation.

sections.label: Neoliberalists versus Reformists debate
sections.summary: The most useful debate is between Neoliberalists who believe in the global free market and Reformists who say global capitalism needs policies for equitable growth.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The most useful debate today is between the Neoliberalists, who overwhelmingly believe in the global free market, and the Reformists, who argue that global capitalism can be a force for good only when accompanied by policies that promote equitable growth, human security and sustainable development.

sections.label: Worker anxiety and S Pass DRC
sections.summary: Workers in their 40s and 50s face income disruption anxiety, and the speaker agrees with reducing the S Pass sub-dependency ratio ceiling in certain industries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Yet, as Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat acknowledges, workers have anxiety, especially those in their 40s and 50s.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Workers in their 40s and 50s are at a stage of their lives when they can least afford income disruption: they have children to raise, mortgages to pay and elderly parents who may be ailing and need financial support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To this end, I agree with the Government's effort in this Budget to boost the hiring of locals and mid-career transitioners, by reducing the S Pass sub-dependency ratio ceiling (DRC) in the Construction, Marine and Process industries.

sections.label: Retrenched man hides job loss
sections.summary: A retrenched man has still not told his wife that he lost his job some months ago.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To illustrate, I know of one retrenched man who has still not told his wife that he lost his job some months ago.

sections.label: CPF savings and redundancy insurance
sections.summary: Measures to consider are more liberal use of CPF savings for education and reskilling, and some form of redundancy insurance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One measure, which I think should be considered, is allowing more liberal use of Central Provident Fund (CPF) savings for education and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This would be reasonable for CPF members whose savings already exceed the applicable Minimum Sums.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Another measure for consideration is some sort of redundancy insurance.

sections.label: Insurance as worker stabiliser
sections.summary: Insurance could stabilise workers and soften job disruption, and ignoring citizen anxiety widens populism and nativism.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today's economic climate illustrates how such insurance could provide a stabiliser to workers, to soften the cliff-edge that they face with job disruption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If the anxiety of citizens is not taken seriously enough, the door to populism and nativism will widen.

sections.label: Falling tourism and driver income
sections.summary: Hotel occupancy fell to 35% or worse, taxi and private hire driver income dipped up to 40%, and attraction visitorship dropped up to 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Just to give Members a sense, hotel occupancy rates have gone down to as low as 35% or worse, from highs of 85% and more.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Our taxi and private hire drivers have given me feedback that income has dipped up to 40%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: And even attractions in Singapore have seen visitorship drop by as much as 90%.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Care Support Packages
sections.summary: The $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package helps businesses defray costs, and the $1.6 billion Care and Support Package addresses workers and other groups.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package announced by the Government will help businesses across industries and specific sectors most affected by the outbreak, to help them defray business costs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The $1.6 billion Care and Support Package shows care for workers and addresses the needs of older workers, young families, the lower-income and our future generations.

sections.label: Company Training Committees progress
sections.summary: A company with about 1,100 workers will customise courses with NTUC Learning Hub, and 352 CTCs have been formed toward a 1,000 goal.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The company is particularly keen to build on their digital roadmap with the help of NTUC Learning Hub to identify and customise relevant courses, such as SkillsFuture for Digital Workplace, for its workforce of about 1,100 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: When we first announced the CTCs last year, the Labour Movement made a goal to have 1,000 CTCs in three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: To date, we have formed 352 CTCs and we are starting to see workers in companies, such as Wildlife Reserves Singapore, reap the benefits of this partnership.

sections.label: NTUC Job Security Council pilot
sections.summary: NTUC is piloting the NTUC JSC to improve matching of displaced or retrenched workers into new jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: NTUC is, therefore, piloting the NTUC JSC, to improve the matching of displaced or retrenched workers into new jobs.

sections.label: Pilot support from tripartite partners
sections.summary: The pilot starts with more than 4,000 companies, supported by the Singapore National Employers Federation and other Trade Associations and Chambers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: The pilot will start with more than 4,000 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: We have strong support from our valued tripartite partner, the Singapore National Employers Federation and many other Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs), such as the Workforce Advancement Federation supporting local small and medium enterprises (SMEs), the Singapore Manufacturing Federation and the Specialists Trade Alliance of Singapore from the building and construction industry.

sections.label: JSC recruitment tool benefits
sections.summary: Companies benefit from a lower-cost ready-made recruitment tool through the JSC, with training and skills upgrading for workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: All these companies will stand to benefit from a lower-cost ready-made recruitment tool through the JSC, with the added bonus of training and skills upgrading for our workers.

sections.label: JSC matching at-risk workers
sections.summary: Through JSC, workers at risk of losing jobs are matched to companies with suitable jobs; over 4,000 companies employing over 500,000 workers are on board, over 90% SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: Through JSC, workers who are at risk of losing their jobs will be matched to companies that have suitable jobs for them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: To date, we have more than 4,000 companies on board the NTUC JSC, employing a total of more than 500,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
sentences.text: More than 90% of these companies are SMEs.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package
sections.summary: The Stabilisation and Support Package announced at Budget 2020 provides assurance and support to businesses and workers amid economic uncertainty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: At a personal level, I am sure the Stabilisation and Support Package announced at Budget 2020 will be a boon to both businesses and workers, as it provides assurance and support in this time of economic uncertainty and ensure every worker matters and every job counts.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up
sections.summary: A $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up for all Singaporeans, which the speaker has lobbied for over the past two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, is the $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up for all Singaporeans, which I have been lobbying for over the past two years.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit creation
sections.summary: The creation of the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit for Employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Third, would be the creation of the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit for Employers.

sections.label: Earlier JSS and SkillsFuture disbursement
sections.summary: The speaker asks if JSS disbursement can be brought forward from July 2020 and if the SkillsFuture Top-up scheduled for October 2020 can be rolled out earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: As such, can the disbursement of JSS be brought forward from the start date of July 2020?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the same vein, many workers, especially the freelance and self-employed, have asked if the SkillsFuture Top-up originally scheduled in October 2020 can be rolled out earlier, so that they can make use of this period of downtime to embark on the relevant training.

sections.label: Support for freelancers and self-employed
sections.summary: The speaker suggests revisiting a scheme to support freelancers and self-employed Singaporeans and asks about extending wage support through sector agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In addition, they were now armed with additional qualifications, such as a Diploma in Hospitality or other related certifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I see a good opportunity for us to revisit and reintroduce this scheme to support workers who may fall through the cracks or those not covered under the current schemes, such as our freelancers and self-employed Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To further support this group of workers, could the Government also look at extending calibrated wage support through sector agencies to help them cope with the immediate impact brought about by the current economic situation?

sections.label: Training incentives amid slowdown
sections.summary: The Government can provide incentives for employers to send workers for training by increasing absentee payroll and course fee funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In light of the current situation, as well as business slowdown for many industries and the possibility of a recession, the Government can step in to provide an additional nudge and incentive for employers to send all their workers for training and skills upgrading through increasing the absentee payroll and course fee funding.

sections.label: Formation of JSC
sections.summary: The speaker's fifth suggestion to ensure job security for workers is the formation of JSC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: To ensure job security for workers, my fifth suggestion would be the formation of JSC.

sections.label: Speeding up JSS disbursement
sections.summary: The speaker suggests speeding up disbursement of JSS and the $500 SkillsFuture Top-up to encourage restructuring, training and upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: First, speed up the disbursement of JSS and the additional $500 SkillsFuture Top-up, encouraging businesses and workers to make use of this period of downtime to restructure, train and upgrade.

sections.label: Changi Airport visitors from China
sections.summary: Changi Airport receives an average of 330,000 visitors from China each month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Our Changi Airport receives an average of 330,000 visitors from China each month.

sections.label: First COVID-19 case in Singapore
sections.summary: On 23 January, Singapore diagnosed its first COVID-19 case, a tourist from Wuhan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: On 23 January, Singapore diagnosed its first case of COVID-19, a tourist from Wuhan.

sections.label: SARS solidarity and NCID stockpile
sections.summary: This solidarity recalls SARS in 2003 with 238 infected and 33 fatalities, since when the NCID and a national face mask stockpile were built.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For many of us in this House, this solidarity reminds us of SARS in 2003 when 238 people were infected with 33 fatalities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Since that time, we have the new National Centre for Infectious Diseases (NCID), we have also built a national stockpile of face masks.

sections.label: Enterprise Transform Package for SMEs
sections.summary: Enterprise Singapore will launch an Enterprise Transform Package focused on leadership, supporting 900 SME business leaders over three years with training and mentorship.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For promising SMEs, the Government has announced that Enterprise Singapore (ESG) will launch an Enterprise Transform Package with focus on leadership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: It will also support business leaders of 900 SMEs over the next three years with training and mentorship.

sections.label: Feedback on COVID-19 SME support gaps
sections.summary: Ground feedback says the July 2020 Job Support Scheme is late, with no extra Absentee Payroll, training subsidies or foreign worker levy waiver for COVID-19 affected enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: First, the ground feedback that I have received is that the Job Support Scheme to be given out in July 2020 is rather late and does little to help mitigate cash flow issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Time is of the essence for these SMEs as the adverse business impact they are facing now due to COVID-19 is a significant one and they are crying out for help with urgency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Second, there is no additional Absentee Payroll and training course subsidies for enterprises affected by COVID-19 to send excess manpower for training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Third, there is no foreign worker levy waiver for enterprises affected by COVID-19, especially when foreign workers represent a significant manpower share in the food services and retail sectors.

sections.label: MOH warning on scam calls
sections.summary: MOH released a statement warning the community about scam calls impersonating the MOH Contact Tracing team to obtain personal financial details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: MOH had to release a statement to warn the community of scam calls impersonating the MOH Contact Tracing team in an attempt to retrieve personal financial details.

sections.label: Government $8.3 billion industry transformation
sections.summary: The Government will invest $8.3 billion to drive industry transformation and develop workers for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The confluence of these factors will impact our entire economy, and I am heartened to note that the Government will be investing $8.3 billion to drive industry transformation and develop our workers for the future.

sections.label: PMET share of retrenchments
sections.summary: MOM retrenchment statistics show the proportion of PMETs among retrenched workers grew from 37% in 2008 to 65% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: According to the retrenchment statistics released by MOM, the proportion of PMETs among workers being retrenched annually has grown from 37% in 2008 to 65% in 2018.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package
sections.summary: The speaker commends Budget 2020's $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package for helping enterprises keep workers during the economic slowdown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: First, I would like to commend Budget 2020 for introducing the Stabilisation and Support Package amounting to $4 billion, which will support our enterprises in keeping their workers during the economic slowdown and position them to rebound quickly once the crisis is over.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-ups for workers
sections.summary: The speaker supports the $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up for mid-career workers aged 40 to 60, but notes it is limited to about 200 selected career transition programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The top-ups will certainly help our workers offset the costs of keeping their skillsets relevant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I also support the $500 special top-up to the SkillsFuture Credit accounts for mid-career workers aged 40 to 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I note, however, that this Special SkillsFuture Credit is limited for use to only about 200 selected career transition programmes.

sections.label: Extending and bringing forward SkillsFuture top-ups
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government extends the Special SkillsFuture Credit top-up to those beyond 60 and urges bringing forward disbursement from 1 October.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Additionally, with our ageing workforce and the corresponding rise in our retirement and re-employment ages, I hope the Government can extend the Special SkillsFuture Credit top-up to those beyond 60 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Like my NTUC colleague, Mr Patrick Tay, I would also urge the Government to bring forward the disbursement of the SkillsFuture Credit top-ups from the current date of 1 October.

sections.label: U PME Centre becoming mobile
sections.summary: The speaker announces that the U PME Centre will evolve into a mobile centre to bring services closer to PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Here, I would like to announce that our U PME Centre will evolve to a mobile centre and bring our services closer to our PMETs.

sections.label: Mobile centres at three CCs
sections.summary: The U PME Centre will set up on-demand mobile centres at three CCs in the Moulmein-Cairnhill constituency: Cairnhill, Tanglin and Pek Kio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: For a start, U PME Centre will set up on-demand mobile centres at the three CCs located within the Moulmein-Cairnhill constituency at Cairnhill, Tanglin and Pek Kio.

sections.label: Partnership for PMET project management workshops
sections.summary: The Labour Movement will work with professional associations and partner the Project Management Institute Singapore Chapter to roll out free project management workshops via the mobile U PME Centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement will, therefore, work with our extensive network of professional associations to equip more PMETs with adaptive skills to improve their employment prospects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am pleased to share that we will be partnering the Project Management Institute Singapore Chapter (SPMI) to roll out free workshops on project management fundamentals through our new mobile U PME Centre.

sections.label: Labour Movement support for workers
sections.summary: The Labour Movement pledges to support all workers and turn crisis into opportunity together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Together, let us continue investing in our people and ensure that our people remain exceptional.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We have weathered through storms and crises before and we will do so again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Regardless of whether you are a fresh graduate, in your mid-career, or in your silver years, the Labour Movement will be there for you because, for us, every worker matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Join us and, together, we can and, together, we will turn crisis into opportunity and emerge stronger and more future-ready than before.

sections.label: COVID-19 supply chain disruption
sections.summary: COVID-19 hits retail, tourism and hospitality, while China factory shutdowns disrupt global supply chains and Singapore manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: While the impact of COVID-19 is most acutely felt in sectors like retail, tourism and hospitality, the prolonged shutdown of factories in China, has disrupted supply chains around the world and the manufacturing sector here in Singapore is not spared from such an impact.

sections.label: Manufacturing firms cut overtime hours
sections.summary: Some manufacturing companies reduce or freeze overtime and plan shorter work weeks, with wage support helping cut costs to save jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As the Deputy Secretary-General of NTUC and the Executive Secretary of the Metal Industries Workers' Union, I get feedback from our management partners that for companies with supply chains that are linked to China factories, there has been a reduction in demand of their products by up to about 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Some manufacturing companies have, therefore, started to reduce or freeze workers' overtime hours while others are planning for a shorter work week if the situation in China does not improve.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Manpower costs are also a significant expenditure for companies, and the wage support measures that are announced during this period will help companies to "cut costs to save jobs" instead of "cutting jobs to save costs".

sections.label: Grants for upskilling and transformation
sections.summary: Enhanced EDG and SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit help companies redesign jobs, upskill workers and transform for economic recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: During a downturn when the volume of work is reduced, the enhanced Enterprise Development Grant (EDG) and the newly announced SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit can help companies to redesign jobs, upskill their workers and look at long-term business transformation so that when economic recovery occurs, companies will be able to swiftly respond and capture new opportunities.

sections.label: NTUC company training committees and A*STAR
sections.summary: 352 companies have formed CTCs, and NTUC partnered A*STAR to train 28 Industry Training Officers for the OTR process.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: As shared by NTUC Secretary-General Mr Ng Chee Meng earlier, to date, we have 352 companies that have formed CTCs across the various industry clusters.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: NTUC has also, in this process, partnered the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) to train a group of 28 Industry Training Officers (ITOs) to conduct the Operations Technology Roadmapping (OTR) process through the CTCs as a platform on which the process can run.

sections.label: US MNC completes OTR process
sections.summary: A US-based MNC with over 500 Singapore workers sought productivity and upskilling, completing the OTR process within a month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The US-based MNC has over 500 workers in their branch here in Singapore and they were looking to increase their productivity, optimise resources and manpower, as well as upskill their workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The company embarked on the OTR process in September last year and, within a month, completed the entire process.

sections.label: EDG and SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit
sections.summary: The enhanced EDG and SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit in this Budget provide funding resources to the tripartite effort to catalyse industry transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: The enhanced EDG and the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit announced in this Budget will provide useful funding resources to this tripartite effort to catalyse industry transformation.

sections.label: Digital transformation and flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: Companies can build digital confidence and make FWAs permanent for some job functions, saving costs and helping working parents balance work and parental duties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Companies can make use of this opportunity to build digital confidence amongst employees and accelerate the digital transformation of their business operations.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: Flexible work arrangements (FWAs) for certain job functions could also be made permanent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: This will not only help companies save on operational costs like office rentals and utilities, but also help many working parents better balance work demands and parental duties, which will encourage more to contribute to our workforce.

sections.label: Budget builds on upskilling efforts
sections.summary: This year's Budget builds on previous efforts to upskill the workforce and transform industries while helping workers, enterprises and the economy through COVID-19 challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development and Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
sentences.text: (In English): Mr Speaker, this year's Budget builds on the previous year's efforts to upskill our workforce and transform our industries while providing crucial help for our workers, our enterprises and our economy to get through the challenges posed by COVID-19.

sections.label: Economic slowdown and Stabilising and Support Package
sections.summary: With 2019 growth of 0.7% and 2020 GDP forecast at -0.5% to 1.5%, the Stabilising and Support Package helps enterprises with wage cost and cash flow pressures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our economy, while fundamentally strong, has slowed down tremendously with an overall growth of just 0.7% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the global trade slowdown and growing uncertainties, the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) has downgraded Singapore's gross domestic product (GDP) to be around -0.5% to 1.5% for 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To deal with the immediate challenge, the proposed Stabilising and Support Package under Budget 2020 will help enterprises with wage cost and cash flow pressures as they grapple with the current economic slowdown.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I applaud JSS, which aims to ensure that our workers stay employed by supporting companies defray their wage cost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will offset 8% of a Singaporean worker's wage, capped at $3,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is estimated to benefit 1.9 million workers.

sections.label: PSA upskilling and reskilling employees
sections.summary: PSA upskills and reskills employees through job redesign, offering mature workers opportunities and alternative employment for Emergency Response personnel upon retirement at 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An example of a forward-thinking company is PSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It has taken active steps to embark on upskilling and reskilling its employees through job redesign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The more mature workers are given similar opportunities and encouraged to upgrade their skills and to adopt technologies so that they continue to contribute productively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, PSA currently offers alternative employment for personnel from the Emergency Response (ER) Team upon retirement at the age of 55.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Working with the union, PSA is encouraging the ER personnel to transit early in their 40s so that they have a longer runway in a new career path while they are in a better position to make the transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Arasu Duraisamy (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While employers do their part, employees themselves need to embrace the culture of continuous upskilling and reskilling.

sections.label: Budget schemes addressing COVID-19 vulnerabilities
sections.summary: The Budget addresses COVID-19 vulnerabilities through schemes such as JSS, tax rebates, bridging loans and rental waivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Budget has addressed these vulnerabilities due to COVID-19 through various schemes, such as JSS, tax rebates, bridging loans, rental waivers and many others.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model support
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Government to support industry stakeholders keen to adopt the Progressive Wage Model so more workers get better wages, skills and productivity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that the Progressive Wage Model (PWM) has shown its effectiveness to help improve workers' skills and wages, I urge the Government to support industry stakeholders if they are keen to adopt PWM so that more workers can enjoy better wages coupled with better skills and increased productivity.

sections.label: Wage benchmarks and employment credit
sections.summary: The speaker proposes occupation and sector wage benchmarks, suggests trialling them in F&B, and welcomes the Enabling Employment Credit for hiring Singaporeans with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Given that wage data are collected in the annual Occupational Wage Survey, we can help these workers by having a wage benchmark by occupation and sector so that workers can identify a fair wage for their occupation and be more aware of the industry standard to make informed decisions about their careers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Perhaps, as a trial to set industry wage benchmark, the tripartite partners could start with the F&B industry where there are around 180,000 workers in diverse roles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I also welcome the Enabling Employment Credit that was announced in the Budget to provide wage offsets to companies hiring Singaporeans with disabilities.

sections.label: Cooling off period for contracts
sections.summary: MOM would consider a cooling off period of up to five working days letting workers rescind signed contracts without penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition, MOM would also want to consider a "cooling off period", perhaps up to five working days, that will allow workers to rescind the contract they have signed, without penalty.

sections.label: Rest areas, SkillsFuture, age discrimination
sections.summary: The speaker suggests excluding rest areas from gross floor area, welcomes SkillsFuture top-ups and the Mid-Career Support Package, and proposes administrative penalties for age discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Perhaps a tipping point that the Government can seriously consider to encourage a higher take-up rate is to allow for rest areas not to be counted as part of the gross floor area (GFA) of a building as the area is usually an unused space or has little commercial value.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This would help many building owners that have already maxed out their GFA to provide a rest area without penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   I welcome all the various top-ups to SkillsFuture and I am especially heartened by the special attention given to mature workers through the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package to help them undergo upskilling and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In addition, we should also consider administrative penalties if employers are guilty of age discriminatory practices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This package will give our older workers greater assurance that they can continue working if they want to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This is a good opportunity for companies to tap on the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant to raise their retirement and re-employment ages ahead of legislative changes.

sections.label: Budget 2020 support for SEPs
sections.summary: Budget 2020 will help self-employed persons as every Singaporean aged 21 and above gets cash support, SkillsFuture Credit and targeted support for tourism-related industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Budget 2020 will help SEPs as every Singaporean 21 years old and above will get cash support, SkillsFuture Credit and targeted support for tourism-related industries.

sections.label: Bargaining power and SEP classification
sections.summary: The proposals are a better balance of bargaining powers, especially for those working with larger entities like platform companies, and classifying SEPs, especially platform workers, as workers under the Employment Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It is one of having better balance of bargaining powers, especially for those working with larger entities, such as the platform companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: And two, to classify SEPs within a limited definition, especially the platform workers, as workers defined by the Employment Act.

sections.label: Gender pay gap study
sections.summary: MOM found women in Singapore earn less than men, with the gap growing from 16% in 2002 to 16.3% in 2018, and an adjusted gap of 6% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: MOM did a study not too long ago and found that women in Singapore are earning less than men today and the gap has grown slightly from 16% in 2002 to 16.3% in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The adjusted gender pay gap was 6% in 2018.

sections.label: Benefits of narrowing gender wage gaps
sections.summary: Studies show gender-equal boards improve firm performance, and evidence shows women and men complement each other, so narrowing wage gaps boosts growth, productivity and equality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Studies have also shown that the financial performance of firms improves with more gender-equal corporate boards…. our evidence – from macroeconomic, sectoral and firm-level data – shows that women and men complement each other in the production process, creating an additional benefit from increasing women's employment on growth." Therefore, the key benefits from narrowing gender wage gaps are: first, a bigger boost to growth; second, higher productivity; and third, a more equal and inclusive society.

sections.label: Flexible work and caregiving burden
sections.summary: Only 47% of Singapore firms offer full-time FWAs, and caregiving disproportionately affects women, with 83.4% of married men employed in 2017 versus 63.3% of married women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Currently, only 47% of firms in Singapore offer full-time FWAs, according to a McKinsey report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: The responsibility of caregiving and housework also continues to disproportionately affect women, who find themselves taking on the double shift of working a job and taking on most of the household responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This added burden of caregiving might have resulted in 83.4% of married men being employed in 2017, compared to 63.3% of married women in the same period of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: First, women should be given the right to FWA post-maternity.

sections.label: Proposed measures for women
sections.summary: Companies should grade women on maternity over eight months rather than 12, and key leadership positions in listed companies should be tracked to prevent gross under-representation of women.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Second, companies should grade women on maternity on an eight-month basis rather than a 12-month basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Third, key leadership positions in our listed companies ought to be tracked and monitored to ensure that women are not being grossly under-represented.

sections.label: PTP drivers' income decline
sections.summary: Over the past month, taxi and private hire drivers said the point-to-point transport industry was badly affected, with incomes plunging and many drivers stopping driving.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Over the past one month, many taxi drivers and private hire drivers told me that the point-to-point (PTP) transport service industry has been badly affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the significant decrease in customers, their incomes have plunged and many drivers have decided to stop driving.

sections.label: Government assistance package for drivers
sections.summary: The Government and operators launched a $77 million assistance package to assist taxi and private hire drivers as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The timely launch of the $77 million assistance package by the Government and operators is also an initiative to assist taxi drivers and private hire drivers as soon as possible.

sections.label: Support for freelance workers
sections.summary: Unions urge the Government to roll out more measures to help freelance workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: On behalf of the unions, I would like to urge the Government again to roll out more measures to help freelance workers.

sections.label: Freelancers' income and training
sections.summary: Freelancers' income plunged, training would mean lost income, but tripartite efforts can keep top talents employed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Their income have plunged due to the decrease in customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Some of these freelancers would like to go for training during this lull period, but are deterred as this would mean a loss of income, so they are also feeling a little helpless.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I believe that with the joint efforts by the tripartite partners, we can ensure that all the top talents in the various industries will be able to keep their jobs, and make use of their talents to enhance Singapore’s competitiveness when the crisis is over.

sections.label: Government support amid COVID-19
sections.summary: The Government will continue to support the economy, companies, workers and families, and tourism should be revived.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although the impact of COVID-19 may not blow over in the short term, the Government will continue to support the economy, companies, workers and families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Hin Kee (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We must remain confident, maintain healthy lifestyles, lead normal lives and try to revive our tourism industry.

sections.label: Raising retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: Tripartite partners agreed to raise retirement age from 62 to 65 and re-employment age from 67 to 70 over a decade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Prime Minister Lee announced at last year's National Day Rally the consensus reached by the tripartite partners to raise retirement age progressively from 62 to 65 and the re-employment age ceiling from 67 to 70 over the course of a decade.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Specific first moves were also announced, namely, to raise retirement age from 62 to 63 and the re-employment age ceiling from 67 to 68 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And one year before that, in 2021, first steps will be taken to raise the CPF contribution rates for workers aged 55 and older.

sections.label: Employer cash grant for local employees
sections.summary: Employers receive an 8% cash grant on gross monthly wages of local employees from October to December 2019, capped at $3,600.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Employers will receive an 8% cash grant on the gross monthly wages of each local employee for the months of October 2019 to December 2019, subject to a monthly wage cap of $3,600 per employee.

sections.label: Hiring incentive for older workers
sections.summary: Employers hiring local jobseekers aged 40 and above get 20% salary support for six months, capped at $6,000 monthly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For older workers who are displaced, there will be a hiring incentive for employers who hire local jobseekers aged 40 and above through a reskilling programme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For each eligible worker, the Government will provide a 20% salary support to the employer for six months, capped at $6,000 a month.

sections.label: SkillsFuture training funding top-ups
sections.summary: More money goes to individuals and companies for training, with SkillsFuture top-ups and a new enterprise grant.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: There will be more money given to individuals and companies to undertake training via SkillsFuture.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: There will be a second top-up of $500 to the SkillsFuture accounts of all Singaporeans aged 25 and above, while middle-age workers will get an additional $500.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: There will also be a new SkillsFuture Enterprise grant to defray up to 90% of companies' business transformation, training and job redesign costs.

sections.label: CTCs formed since inception
sections.summary: 352 CTCs have been formed since its inception in April last year, with good progress made.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Good progress has been made in this area, and again, as reported earlier, 352 CTCs have already been formed since its inception in April last year.

sections.label: Mid-career support job placement
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Mid-career Support Package will double job placement of professionals via the PCPs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: In this Budget, through the SkillsFuture Mid-career Support Package, the Government is going to double the job placement of professionals via the PCPs.

sections.label: Labour Movement on striving
sections.summary: The Labour Movement stands ready to work with Government and employers to tackle the tough patch and build better futures.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I heard our Deputy Prime Minister over the radio as he was discussing aspects of the Budget and exhorting everybody to keep our spirits up and together do our best, and he quoted the name of a Hokkien song title.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: He said, “要 拼 才 会 赢”, which means in English, success comes through effort and striving.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Success will not come from just taking painkillers or hunkering down.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: It will come from taking action – concrete, purposeful, effective action.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement stands ready to work with the Government and employers to tackle this tough patch and to simultaneously build that better future of better wages, welfare and work prospects for all workers.

sections.label: CSA, EVs, climate measures
sections.summary: Proposed measures include a bigger CSA Budget, replacing internal combustion engine vehicles with EVs by 2040, and climate change mitigation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Among the proposed measures which, for me, deserves special mention are increasing the Budget for CSA to embark on new capabilities needed to protect our information technology (IT) systems against increasingly sophisticated attacks, removing the internal combustion engine vehicles by 2040 and replacing them with electric vehicles (EVs), and measures to mitigate the effects of climate change.

sections.label: SARS response and preparations
sections.summary: The response to SARS in 2003 and subsequent preparations for the next crisis have stood us well.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Our response to the SARS episode in 2003 and subsequent changes we made to prepare for the next crisis have stood us well in this instance.

sections.label: POFMA dissent stifling debate
sections.summary: POFMA is being debated, with some viewing it as an attempt to stifle dissent on the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Another issue of trust currently being debated is POFMA as some view this as an attempt to stifle dissent on the Internet.

sections.label: Licensing online news sites 2013
sections.summary: Licensing online news sites in 2013 was alleged to kill Internet diversity, but it did not stifle the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: When I moved to license online news sites in 2013, several Internet groups alleged that this move would kill the diversity of voices on the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: As it turns out, the licensing scheme did not stifle the Internet at all.

sections.label: PDPA and data protection concerns
sections.summary: PDPA protects personal data, but newer laws and the Government's carved-out handling of citizens data may raise privacy and accountability issues.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) has put in place several measures to protect personal data, but the emergence of data protection legislation that favours more to data owners, such as the European Union General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and California Consumer Privacy Act, will cause some to wonder whether PDPA is sufficiently rigorous to protect personal data.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Similarly, since the Government's handling of citizens data is carved out from PDPA, a time will come when some will raise issues of privacy and accountability.

sections.label: Independent Digital Commission proposal
sections.summary: Following AI guidelines released by the Ministry of Communications and Information, a community conversation and an independent Digital Commission are suggested.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Just like the guidelines for the use of AI which have been released by the Ministry of Communications and Information in Davos earlier this year, perhaps there is a need for a community wide conversation on how these technologies should be deployed.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Should we not consider the creation of an independent Digital Commission that looks at these concerns from all sides dispassionately?

sections.label: Bioethics Advisory Committee created
sections.summary: When human biomedical research raised concerns, the Bioethics Advisory Committee was created to advise the Government.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: When human biomedical research raised some concerns, we created the Bioethics Advisory Committee to advise the Government on these matters.

sections.label: New norms after pandemic
sections.summary: It is early to think of closure, but the nation can adopt new hygiene, work-life, technology and attitude norms.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is still early for us to think of such projects of closure.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But one thing we can do as a nation is to adopt new norms of hygiene standards, work-life balance arrangements, more adoption of technological ways of doing things, such as running online classes and meetings, and other reasonable practices that can become our new way of life.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I would add one more change and, that is, of our attitude towards those at the frontline in fighting this challenge.

sections.label: Dignity of every worker
sections.summary: The dignity of every worker must be maintained and cherished, and this legacy should become part of our enduring character.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The dignity of every worker, no matter their occupation and station in life, must forever be maintained and cherished by all of us.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Let us show to the world that these attitudes and behaviours are not a flash in the pan, but an integral part of our way of life.

sentences.speaker: Prof Yaacob Ibrahim (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: This is the legacy I hope we can bestow on succeeding generations that, out of this moment in our history, our better half triumphed over the other half and it became part of our enduring character.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package praised
sections.summary: The Stabilisation and Support Package was put together with agility and speed to help sectors hit by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Commendable are the agility and speed by which the Stabilisation and Support Package was put together to help sectors hit by COVID-19; the empathy to delay the GST increase this year, and the ability to keep an eye on both the short- and longer-term concerns of Singaporeans and businesses.

sections.label: Worry over large deficits
sections.summary: Many are relieved the Government delayed the GST increase and ran a larger deficit, but worry how long such deficits can be sustained.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Many people are relieved and thankful that the Government acted swiftly to delay the expected GST increase and boldly decided on a larger than expected Budget deficit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: But even with the Deputy Prime Minister's recent public assurance that the Government is prepared to do more if warranted, many people are nonetheless still worried about how long the Government will be able to sustain deficits of such a large quantum.

sections.label: Enterprises and workforce share
sections.summary: In Singapore, they make up 99% of total enterprises and employ more than 70% of the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: In Singapore, they make up 99% of total enterprises and employ more than 70% of the workforce.

sections.label: Requests on Budget measures
sections.summary: Some ask for Budget measures to be administered more expediently and for measures like job support to be extended to six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Some are asking for administration of Budget measures to be more expedient and some ask for the extension of measures, such as job support, to be extended to six months.

sections.label: Household income inequality lowest
sections.summary: The Department of Statistics reported household income inequality in 2019 was at its lowest in almost two decades.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Income inequality is a hot topic for many societies, including Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is, indeed, good news that our Department of Statistics reported that household income inequality as in 2019 was at its lowest in almost two decades, with a lower Gini coefficient of 0.452 versus 0.458 the year before, and even lower at 0.398 after adjusting for Government transfers, such as Workfare and GST rebates.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit first tranche usage
sections.summary: About 500,000 citizens used SkillsFuture Credit in the first tranche, roughly 20% of the resident labour force.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The 500,000 or so citizens who tapped on their SkillsFuture Credit in the first tranche works out to be only about 20% of the resident labour force.

sections.label: SG Together nation-building cornerstone
sections.summary: In January 2020 the Deputy Prime Minister called SG Together the new cornerstone of nation-building and a partnership model.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister, in January 2020, called SG Together the "new cornerstone of nation-building", a new model of partnership between the Government and Singaporeans in owning, shaping and acting on our future to expand what is called the "democracy of deeds".

sections.label: Transport Ministry and connectivity
sections.summary: The Ministry of Transport is no longer dealing with just transportation but connectivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Transport is no longer dealing with just transportation but connectivity.

sections.label: Government trusting people less controllably
sections.summary: The people have long trusted the Government, and it is time for the Government to trust the people less controllably and more facilitatively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The people of Singapore has trusted the Government for so long, it is time for the Government to also learn to trust the people, too – not blindly, not indiscriminately, but in a less controlling and more facilitative manner.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It can end up as a lofty aspiration, but if done right, it will be a powerful driver to a stronger Singapore that can weather many storms heavier than COVID-19 or more tragic crises.

sections.label: Retiree couple pre-Budget 2020 illustration
sections.summary: A Budget Annex illustration showed a retiree couple, both 65, with only $570 a month pre-Budget 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: In the illustration given in the Budget Annex, a retiree couple, both 65 years old, had only $570 a month in total to support their retirement needs, pre-Budget 2020.

sections.label: CPF Basic Retirement Sum shortfall
sections.summary: A study said those 65 and above need at least $1,379 monthly, and 30% of 2021 and 2022 cohorts cannot live on CPF payouts alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: What if this couple does not have family support and savings?

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: There was a study released by two professors last year in which an elderly person aged 65 and above would need at least $1,379 a month to sustain a basic standard of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: With the CPF system being the bedrock of our retirement plans, the Government expects seven-in-10 active CPF members from the 2021 and 2022 cohorts to be able to set aside their Basic Retirement Sum (BRS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: That would mean that 30% of the members in these cohorts would not be able to live on their CPF payouts alone when they reach their Payout Eligibility Age (PEA) in 10 years’ time.

sections.label: Expanded lifelong wage criteria
sections.summary: Expanded lifelong wage criteria are expected to benefit about 100,000 more Singaporeans aged 65 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The expanded criteria for lifelong wages from $70,000 to $140,000 in total CPF contributions and household monthly income per person are expected to benefit about 100,000 more Singaporeans aged 65 and above.

sections.label: Singapore aid to China
sections.summary: Singapore dispatched a second round of humanitarian aid to China last week, and common humanity must prevail.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: The sooner China recovers, the better it will be for all.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: So, it is heartening for me to read that Singapore has dispatched a second round of humanitarian aid to China last week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
sentences.text: It is important that, in moments like this, a sense of common humanity that transcends border, race, language or religion must prevail.

sections.label: Cheaper, better, faster through skills
sections.summary: Singapore tries to be cheaper, better and faster by raising skills, productivity and business capabilities, not lowering wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: In short, we try to be cheaper, better, faster, not by lowering wages, but by raising skills and productivity and developing new business capabilities, so that we can command higher wages for our people, and higher premium for our businesses.

sections.label: Three out of three growth
sections.summary: Singapore has consistently achieved economic, employment and wage growth, three out of three, decade after decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: Out of the three types of growth – economic growth, employment growth and wage growth – many countries could achieve may be one out of three, or two out of three.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: But for Singapore, we have achieved three out of three, consistently, decade after decade.

sections.label: Social cohesion through social transfers
sections.summary: Nation-building aims at social cohesion, countered with social transfers, MediShield Life, PGP and MGP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: Our end objective in nation-building has always been social cohesion, not economic growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: This is why we counter social divides with social transfers, billions of dollars in every term of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: We counter rising healthcare cost with MediShield Life for all and we take extra care of our seniors with the Pioneer Generation Package (PGP) and Merdeka Generation Package (MGP).

sections.label: Neither divided nor less competitive
sections.summary: Singapore wants neither globalisation with a divided society nor deglobalisation with a less competitive economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: What we want is neither globalisation with a divided society, nor deglobalisation with a less competitive economy.

sections.label: National AI Strategy launch
sections.summary: The National AI Strategy gives Singapore a national platform to innovate with AI faster and exploit AI better.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: With the recent launch of the National AI Strategy, we now have a national platform to innovate with AI faster and exploit AI better.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model and upskilling
sections.summary: The PWM's four ladders can transform low-wage jobs and workers, and the speaker urges wider adoption, higher retirement ages and SkillsFuture upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Progressive Wage Model (PWM) has four ladders of job, skill, productivity and wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: It can help transform every low-wage job into a better job, every low-wage worker into a better worker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: I urge our 4G leadership to widen and deepen the adoption of PWM more proactively and more passionately to many more jobs in many more sectors so that the social divide of "High versus Low" can be turned into the social unity of "High and Low", moving up our employment ladder together.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: Retirement age and re-employment age are set to move up progressively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under SkillsFuture, we are doing much more to upskill and reskill our people.

sections.label: Singapore under 3G leaders
sections.summary: Singapore has continued to grow from strength to strength from the first to the current 3G leaders under the "da wo" leadership style.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: From the first to the current 3G leaders, Singapore has continued to grow from strength to strength under the "da wo" leadership style.

sections.label: Heng Swee Keat's caring heart
sections.summary: Minister Mentor said Heng Swee Keat has one of the best brains in Singapore, and the speaker saw his caring heart at a dinner.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: Minister Mentor once said Heng Swee Keat has one of the best brains in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: And what came across clearly and strongly for me from that over four-hour dinner was that he also has one of the most caring hearts for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sections.label: 4G leadership and national ownership
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister wants 4G leaders to engage, consult and rally Singaporeans to forge shared national ownership of future development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: Under his leadership, it is loud and clear to me that the Deputy Prime Minister wants the 4G leaders to do even better, to do even more – engaging with Singaporeans, consulting them, rallying them to contribute ideas and act in concert, because he wants to forge a national ownership that is shared by all Singaporeans in the future development of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: I am heartened that our 4G leadership not only knows a lot about challenges in nation-building but also cares a lot about the sentiment, anxiety, aspiration and inspiration of our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say (East Coast)
sentences.text: I urge everyone in this House, and all our fellow Singaporeans, let us all put our hearts, our heads and our hands together, to jointly create our future Singapore, one that is more globally competitive, more locally cohesive and more sustainable with unlimited potential.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package help
