sections.summary: The $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package helps businesses with cash flow and jobs support, and the speaker requests earlier JSS disbursement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package will be a great help to businesses, with cash flow and jobs support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: JSS offers temporary wage offsetting, the Wage Credit Scheme enhancement co-funds wage increases and the extended Adapt and Grow Initiative will boost training and reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would just like to request that the Finance Minister consider disbursing the JSS payments earlier than the targeted date of end-July.

sections.label: Support for connected businesses
sections.summary: The speaker appeals for support for businesses connected to tourism, aviation, retail, food services and point-to-point transport, noting funds are limited and amounts must be impactful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Funds are limited and the amounts must be large enough to be impactful.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I appeal for some support for businesses connected to the five supported sectors of tourism, aviation, retail, food services and point-to-point transport services as well.

sections.label: Hiring incentive for employers
sections.summary: The proposed hiring incentive gives employers 20% salary support for six months, and the speaker hopes the Government will monitor its effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The proposed hiring incentive for employers, which provides 20% salary support to the employers for six months, is attractive and I hope the Government will monitor its effectiveness.

sections.label: Assistance for taxi relief drivers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry of Transport could consider extending an assistance scheme to support taxi relief drivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry of Transport consider extending such an assistance scheme to support taxi relief drivers?

sections.label: Reserves and Net Investment Returns Contribution
sections.summary: The passage credits predecessors for building Reserves and assets providing the Net Investment Returns Contribution, expected to remain the top revenue contributor this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We thank our predecessors for their thrift and wisdom in building up our Reserves and assets which provide the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC).

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This year's NIRC is expected to remain the top contributor to our revenue, ahead of corporate and personal income tax and GST.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Care Support Packages
sections.summary: The $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package and $1.6 billion Care and Support Package will substantially help businesses and households with short-term challenges.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package and $1.6 billion Care and Support Package will provide substantial help to businesses and households to deal with the short-term challenges ahead.

sections.label: Social and Family Development expenditure
sections.summary: The speaker says the topic is close to their heart and that Social and Family Development expenditure is expected to rise 8.5% to $3.3 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is a topic very close to my heart.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This year, the expenditure for Social and Family Development is expected to increase by 8.5% to $3.3 billion.

sections.label: SSO customised social service manpower
sections.summary: The SSO provides customised social service for each distressed resident or family, and its resources, especially manpower, are stretched.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The SSO provides a customised social service, catering to the different requirements of each distressed resident or family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This is labour-intensive work and, not surprisingly, our SSOs are very much stretched in terms of resources, specifically manpower.

sections.label: Delegating follow-up to free SSO officers
sections.summary: Delegating follow-up work to someone like Mr Ho, with a system in place, could free SSO officers for earlier coordination and intervention work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: If this follow-up portion can be delegated to people like Mr Ho, someone who loves people, enjoys working with people and who has such invaluable experience and, if a system can be put in place, the SSO officers can be freed up to do the earlier coordination and intervention work.

sections.label: EV Early Adoption Incentive rebate
sections.summary: DPM Heng Swee Keat announced phasing out ICE vehicles by 2040, with an EV Early Adoption Incentive giving a 45% ARF rebate capped at $20,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat announced the vision to phase out Internal Combustion Engine (ICE) vehicles and for all vehicles to run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: One of the measures to push more people to buy EVs is the introduction of the EV Early Adoption Incentive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This is a 45% rebate on the Additional Registration Fee (ARF), capped at $20,000.

sections.label: Hyundai Ioniq Electric price premium
sections.summary: A Hyundai Ioniq Electric currently sells for $152,000, a $44,000 premium over its hybrid sibling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For instance, a Hyundai Ioniq Electric currently sells for $152,000, a premium of $44,000 over its hybrid sibling.

sections.label: Eight EV car models available
sections.summary: A check among mainstream car brands sold here found only eight EV car models for consumers to choose from.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A check among the mainstream car brands sold here indicated that there are only eight EV car models which consumers can choose from.

sections.label: ICE tax on car dealers
sections.summary: Car dealers unable to meet the target can be levied a $5,000 ICE tax on every ICE car model they sell.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: For car dealers who are unable to meet the target, a $5,000 ICE tax can be levied on every ICE car model which they sell.

sections.label: PAP Town Councils business continuity plans
sections.summary: The 15 People's Action Party Town Councils are reviewing their business continuity plans, developed since last year using ISO 22301 standards.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: At this juncture, I wish to share that the 15 People's Action Party Town Councils are reviewing their respective BCPs to ensure that they are kept operational even during times of crises.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Last year, we started to develop our BCP framework in accordance with international standards, that is, the International Organization for Standardization (ISO) 22301, to ensure that the plans are objectively consistent, credible and viable.

sections.label: Clean Toilets @ North West project
sections.summary: In January 2020, the North West Community Development Council implemented a project to transform all toilets at coffee shops.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In January 2020, the North West Community Development Council (CDC) implemented a project named "Clean Toilets @ North West" to transform all toilets at coffee shops.

sections.label: Bukit Panjang coffee shop toilet upgrades
sections.summary: Clean Toilet project details are on North West CDC's website, and all Bukit Panjang coffee shop operators agreed to upgrade toilets to the new benchmark.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Details of the Clean Toilet project can be downloaded from North West CDC’s website.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: We are pleased to note that all the coffee shop operators in Bukit Panjang have agreed to upgrade their toilets to meet this new benchmark.

sections.label: South Korean Restroom Reform outcome
sections.summary: The transformation has been permanent and successful, with South Korean toilets among the cleanest 26 years after the Restroom Reform began.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The transformation has been permanent and successful, with South Korean toilets continuing to be some of the cleanest in the world, 26 years after the start of the South Korean Restroom Reform.

sections.label: Emergency preparedness app and endowment fund
sections.summary: An app gives crisis preparedness and response guidance, and the speaker urges the Finance Minister to consider an Emergency Preparedness Endowment Fund.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It is imperative that we equip our people with the knowledge and skills to survive and to help others during a crisis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This app provides an emergency preparedness and response protocol guide for 14 crisis scenarios, such as fire, flood, bomb threats or infectious disease outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It also has an illustrated first-aid guide, an emergency bag inventory checklist, a resource directory covering clinics, polyclinics, hospitals, police stations, civil defence shelters, community centres and emergency telephone numbers which Singaporeans can call to seek assistance when in Singapore or in the 10 most frequently travelled overseas destinations by Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: By having this app downloaded by these users, we can build a 4.7 million-strong community of lifesavers.

sentences.speaker: Dr Teo Ho Pin (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In this regard, I would urge the Finance Minister to consider setting up an Emergency Preparedness Endowment Fund to continually train all Singaporeans to be prepared for crises which may occur in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: One that resonated with me, which is worth repeating in this House, is that it is exceptional for a government to achieve real wage growth, real employment growth and economic growth, all at the same time.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit suggestion
sections.summary: The speaker's next suggestion involves the Enabling Employment Credit (EEC).

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: My next suggestion involves the Enabling Employment Credit (EEC).

sections.label: Credit for ex-offender employers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a similar credit could be provided to employers of ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Returning to the point I want to make: I wonder if a similar credit could be provided to employers of ex-offenders?

sections.label: EEC incentives for ex-offenders
sections.summary: The speaker notes a salary seldom above $800 a month and asks if EEC could be extended to incentivise employers to employ ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: His salary seldom goes beyond $800 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I wonder if EEC could be extended to provide incentives to employers to employ or give full employment to ex-offenders.

sections.label: EVs and ICE phase-out
sections.summary: Mr Yee Chia Hsing spoke about EVs, and the Deputy Prime Minister has a vision of phasing out ICE vehicles by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: On the clarification, Mr Yee Chia Hsing spoke about EVs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I note the Deputy Prime Minister's bold vision of phasing out ICE vehicles and having all vehicles run on cleaner energy by 2040.

sections.label: Vehicle lot conversion and EV tax
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a transparent, demand-driven model for conversion of lots and notes a contemplated lump sum tax for EVs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Going forward, it may be better for a transparent, demand-driven model for conversion of lots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Next, on the vehicular tax structure, I note that the Deputy Prime Minister is contemplating a lump sum tax for EVs to account for loss in fuel excise duties.

sections.label: Consultation and Unity Budget
sections.summary: The speaker says about 1,000 leaders were engaged and their ideas incorporated into this Budget, which crossed the $100-billion mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This reflects the extent of consultation that Deputy Prime Minister Heng and his colleagues engaged with people on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I understand from his speech that about 1,000 leaders from different parts of society were engaged and their ideas were incorporated into this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Truly, this is a "Unity" Budget from conception.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I do not recall many other Budgets crossing this $100-billion mark.

sections.label: Start of term figure
sections.summary: The speaker states that at the start of the term of Government this year, it was about $64 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: At the start of the term of Government this year, it was about $64 billion.

sections.label: Payment deadline for eligible employees
sections.summary: Eligible employees will receive payment by 31 July 2020 for wages paid from October to December 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Eligible employees will receive the payment by 31 July 2020 for wages paid out from the months of October to December 2019.

sections.label: Outreach on rebate savings
sections.summary: It asks whether any outreach was done in past years to determine how much rebate savings are passed to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Has any outreach been done in the past years to determine how much of the savings from the rebates are passed on to the tenants?

sections.label: Waiver of Foreign Worker Levy
sections.summary: It asks whether a Foreign Worker Levy waiver can be introduced for five directly affected sectors and other struggling industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Will it be possible to introduce a waiver of the Foreign Worker Levy for the five directly affected sectors as well as other industries which are not doing so well?

sections.label: Off-Budget package and job placements
sections.summary: It asks if enough exists for an off-Budget package in a protracted pandemic, and notes a aim to double annual job placements of locals in their 40s and 50s to around 5,500 by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In the alternate worst-case scenario of a protracted global pandemic situation, can the Deputy Prime Minister share with us if we have enough to undertake an off Budget package, if needed, to help businesses and workers?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister has highlighted the aim to double the annual job placement of locals in their 40s and 50s to around 5,500 by the year 2025 via increasing the capacity of reskilling programmes, such as the PCP under the Adapt and Grow initiative, plus other sector-specific and career transition programmes.

sections.label: Enhancing Capability Transfer Programme
sections.summary: Last year the speaker proposed enhancing the Capability Transfer Programme to incentivise companies to train more local workforce through overseas training or foreign specialists.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Last year, I proposed in my Adjournment Motion to the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices and MOM to enhance the Capability Transfer Programme (CTP) to incentivise companies to train more of their local workforce by sending them for training overseas or have them trained under a foreign specialist with the aim of transferring or sharing the new job scope.

sections.label: Rising food prices and import costs
sections.summary: Since 2013 food prices rose about 10%, with 2019 seeing the fastest increase in a decade, and a weaker Singapore dollar will raise import costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Since 2013, food prices have gone up by about 10%, while 2019 saw the fastest increase in food prices in a decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With the Singapore dollar hitting a three-year low against the United States (US) dollar and weakening against regional currencies, costs of our imports will go up.

sections.label: Care and Support Package
sections.summary: The $1.6 billion Care and Support Package helps Singaporean households defray household expenses via cash outlays and special Workfare payments amid rising healthcare costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Despite all the existing measures and schemes to keep healthcare costs affordable even for the very poor, it is apparent that healthcare costs will keep going up with the increased demand for better-skilled healthcare workers and medical equipment and pricing power of the pharmaceutical companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, the announced $1.6 billion Care and Support Package provides assurance and support to Singaporean households during this period of uncertainty, by helping to defray some of their household expenses via various cash outlays, special Workfare payments and others.

sections.label: Profiteering and price adjustments
sections.summary: The speaker suggests a single enforcement unit to address profiteering and asymmetric price adjustments, and notes household income inequality was at its lowest in almost two decades.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: One avenue that comes to mind is to ensure that we have adequate measures for a start to monitor as a whole-of-Government to ensure prices of food, necessities and energy-related products do not see profiteering and asymmetric price adjustments that could affect general households during periods of crisis or shocks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But typically, when you adjust prices lower, energy companies tend to take a lag effect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: So, besides the MTI-related workgroup and committees, the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) and Competition Commission of Singapore (CCCS) looking at profiteering, can we set up a single enforcement unit to address profiteering and price adjustment asymmetries in a more sustained manner or embed it more explicitly to address inefficient pricing practices within the CCCS mandate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A Department of Statistics' Key Household Income Trends report states that household income inequality here last year was at its lowest in almost two decades.

sections.label: Assistance for social enterprises
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government has done outreach to social enterprises, how effective they have been in employing the vulnerable, and whether closer cooperation is possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Has the Government done any outreach to social enterprises to find out what kind of assistance they need?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How effective have social enterprises been in offering sustainable and stable employment to the vulnerable group?

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Can the Government work more closely with social enterprises to uplift this vulnerable group?

sections.label: Prolonged U-shape economy
sections.summary: A prolonged U-shape economic situation is becoming more likely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A prolonged U-shape economic situation is becoming more likely.

sections.label: Monthly meetings with TACs
sections.summary: For the next 12 months, MOF, MTI and MOM can have monthly meetings with the key TACs and unions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: One, for the next 12 months, MOF, MTI and MOM can have monthly meetings with the key TACs and unions.

sections.label: IRAS Jobs Support Programme
sections.summary: IRAS can consider implementing the Jobs Support Programme immediately, and some deeply impacted companies are asking for a short-term waiver of the Foreign Worker Levy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Some ideas – the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) can also consider implementing the Jobs Support Programme for them immediately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Some deeply impacted companies are asking for a short-term waiver of the Foreign Worker Levy.

sections.label: Second economic package question
sections.summary: Some Singaporeans are wondering whether there will be a second economic package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Lastly, some Singaporeans are wondering if there will be a second economic package.

sections.label: Healthcare supply chain resilience review
sections.summary: Global circumstances require an immediate review of Singapore's medical stockpile and resilience policy, and if necessary anchoring relevant manufacturers here on strategic considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yet, over the years, the global healthcare supply chain has become overly lean for even crucial healthcare essentials.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to WHO, the widespread inappropriate use of face masks and protective suits globally by those not at the frontline caring for patients, further contributed to the unexpected shortage and price surge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Therefore, changing global circumstances require us to do an immediate review of our medical stockpile and resilience policy, both for basic drugs and medical disposables commonly used in pandemics.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If necessary, we should anchor relevant manufacturers in Singapore on strategic and not purely economic considerations.

sections.label: Possible sudden revenue drop
sections.summary: If these developments take place, the impact on the revenue base could be swift and sizable, with lost corporate income tax and other losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If these developments take place, the impact on our revenue base could be swift and sizable – billions of dollars of lost corporate income tax, additional spending to keep and attract current and future investments, loss tax revenue and spending by a reduced international workforce, and less job opportunities for our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that within this Chamber, as we discuss about meeting current and future needs, we can keep in mind the possibility of a sudden revenue drop.

sections.label: Wage, cash flow and rental relief
sections.summary: Wage and enterprise cash flow relief measures will help, and SMF hopes for a more structured framework for rental relief directly to tenants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Wage relief in the form of the New JSS and the Enhanced Wage Credit Scheme, as well as enterprise cash flow relief in the form of Corporate Tax Rebates and enhancement of the Enterprise Financing Scheme, will go some way towards assuaging society’s fear of lost livelihoods and shuttered enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: SMF is also glad that the Government has taken on board the feedback from our members and stated that Government landlords are willing to exercise some form of flexibility with rentals during this difficult time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, while the above is indeed welcomed, the community wishes that the Deputy Prime Minister can consider going further by providing a more structured framework for rental relief which provides for more immediate relief directly to the tenants, rather than through the landlords.

sections.label: Relief measures efficacy timeline
sections.summary: Many are optimistic the economy will show recovery in six months, so relief measures should factor in an efficacy timeline of six months to a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, many are optimistic that the economy will start to show signs of recovery six months from now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would, therefore, be commensurating with such expectations and hope that relief measures factor in an efficacy timeline of between six months to a year.

sections.label: Workforce transformation and training courses
sections.summary: SMF created a course on business models towards Industry 4.0 and is the first Programme Manager for the Professional Conversion Programme to achieve 1,000 placements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Where workforce transformation and training are concerned, SMF has recently created a course to help businesses examine their business models and identify ways of changing these models towards Industry 4.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We are focusing on facilitating mid-career switches and are the first Programme Manager for the Professional Conversion Programme (Broad-based) to achieve 1,000 placements.

sections.label: Manufacturing DRC and manpower concerns
sections.summary: The Government's $8.3 billion allocation is welcomed, and the manufacturing community hopes for more lead time if the DRC decrease is implemented.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The commitment by the Government to allocate $8.3 billion in this Budget to drive Singapore’s transformation and growth strategy is, indeed, heartening as it will continue to support the work and initiatives of TACs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One concern which the manufacturing community has from Deputy Prime Minister Heng's speech is that of the superseded decrease in the DRC for the manufacturing sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The community is relieved that the Government has prudently decided not to implement such a measure in such difficult times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, there is always an innate and recurring fear of the shortage of suitable local manpower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Douglas Foo (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is the community’s hope that if and when the Government decides to effect the decrease in the DRC for the manufacturing sector, more lead time can be given for our members to prepare and plan ahead.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package jobs support
sections.summary: Of the $4 billion package, $2.4 billion goes to JSS and the enhanced Wage Credit Scheme, with $1.3 billion injected to keep 1.9 million local employees employed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Of the $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package, a whopping 60%, or $2.4 billion, will go towards JSS and the enhanced Wage Credit Scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Jobs Support will provide companies an 8% cash grant based on the gross monthly wages of their local employees for three months, subject to a monthly wage cap of $3,600 per employee.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Over the next three months, the Government will inject about $1.3 billion to employers and help keep 1.9 million local employees in their jobs.

sections.label: Enhanced scheme qualifying salary raised
sections.summary: The enhanced scheme raised the qualifying salary from $4,000 to $5,000, with $1.1 billion going to about 90,000 employers and over 700,000 local employees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The enhanced scheme has also raised the qualifying salary from $4,000 to $5,000, with $1.1 billion going to about 90,000 employers, benefiting more than 700,000 local employees.

sections.label: S Pass quota cuts for sectors
sections.summary: Cuts in S Pass quotas for construction, marine and process sectors are forthcoming, with these sectors given a longer period to adjust.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In addition, after much careful consideration, we have announced forthcoming cuts in the S Pass quotas for construction, marine and process sectors, but we will give these sectors a longer period to adjust.

sections.label: Agencies help employers reach recruits
sections.summary: Workforce Singapore and SkillsFuture Singapore work with agencies like the Building and Construction Authority to help employers reach fresh graduates and mid-career switchers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For all these reasons, Workforce Singapore and SkillsFuture Singapore have been working closely with agencies like the Building and Construction Authority to help employers reach out to fresh graduates as well as mid-career switchers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Employers, too, can help themselves by enhancing job quality and widening the pool of potential recruits.

sections.label: Job attractiveness and business transformation
sections.summary: Efforts to make jobs more attractive to skilled Singaporeans go with business transformation, and waiving or cutting levies would blunt motivation to restructure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: I hope that SMF, of which he is the President, will help them to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: These efforts to make jobs more attractive to skilled Singaporeans go hand-in-hand with an overall emphasis on business transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Waiving or cutting levies would blunt the motivation to restructure, improve job quality and become more manpower-lean.

sections.label: Hotel housekeeping efficiency measures
sections.summary: Housekeepers are notified of ready rooms via mobile app, bedding changes cut tidying time 20%, and a new vacuuming system halved job time.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For example, housekeepers no longer waste time knocking on doors to figure out which room was ready to be cleaned and are instead notified through a mobile app.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Bedding was changed so that it takes 20% less time to tidy up each room.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: A new vacuuming system has halved the time to get the job done.

sections.label: Tourism sector support package
sections.summary: A multi-agency support package worth over $15 million involving tripartite partners helps tourism businesses use downtime for training and transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Instead of levy reductions or waivers, we have put together a multi-agency support package worth more than $15 million that also involves our tripartite partners, for businesses in the tourism sector to use the downtime for more training and transformation.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credits for employers and employees
sections.summary: Employers can access SkillsFuture Enterprise Credits up to $10,000 while employees receive SkillsFuture Credit top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The employers can now access SkillsFuture Enterprise Credits up to $10,000 while the employees themselves have SkillsFuture Credit top-ups.

sections.label: Stability and Support Package funds
sections.summary: Of the $4 billion Stability and Support Package in this year's Budget, 60% of funds will help Singaporeans retain their jobs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   Mr Deputy Speaker, of the $4 billion Stability and Support Package in this year's Budget, 60% of the funds will be used to help Singaporeans retain their jobs.

sections.label: Foreign Worker Levy position
sections.summary: Levies have not been raised since 2016 for most sectors and are waived for employees under Leave of Absence, Stay-Home Notice or Quarantine Order.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The fact is that since 2016, levies have not been raised for the vast majority of sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Apart from that, levies are waived for employees under Leave of Absence, Stay-Home Notice or Quarantine Order.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We do not intend to reduce or waive the Foreign Worker Levy across the board because of two key reasons.

sections.label: Temporary foreign worker transfer scheme
sections.summary: SBF will administer a temporary scheme to help excess foreign workers transfer to employers with manpower shortages.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For employers with excess foreign workers, SBF will also administer a temporary scheme to help the workers to be transferred to employers with manpower shortages.

sections.label: Mid-career professionals job difficulties
sections.summary: Feedback indicates some mid-career professionals using Adapt and Grow Schemes still struggle to find jobs after some time.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: On the ground, we are getting feedback that some of the mid-career professionals who try to tap on the existing Adapt and Grow Schemes are still finding difficulties getting a job after some time.

sections.label: MOM PMET employment outcomes report
sections.summary: MOM published a report showing PMET employment outcomes over the last 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Not long ago, MOM published a report which shows over the last 10 years what the employment outcomes have been for PMETs.

sections.label: Sustaining job creation momentum
sections.summary: It is important to sustain the momentum of job creation.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: First, it is really important to sustain the momentum of job creation.

sections.label: Motivation for individual upskilling
sections.summary: It is important to maintain individuals' motivation to keep upskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The second, which is also very important, is to maintain a sense of motivation on the part of individuals to keep upskilling.

sections.label: Promoting fair employment practices
sections.summary: Fair Employment must keep being promoted so businesses recruit openly and fairly without discriminating, especially against locals and older workers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Third, it is important to keep promoting Fair Employment, promotion of Fair Employment, letting businesses know that they have to keep recruitment open and to consider all candidates fairly and not discriminate against anyone, particularly our locals, particularly those who are not necessarily so young anymore.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit effectiveness questions
sections.summary: The Budget's overseas exposure funding is welcomed, but the effectiveness of SkillsFuture credit top-ups and the career-switch percentage among users are questioned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Budget set aside to prepare our youths to be more globally ready through overseas exposure is also a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask for the effectiveness of the SkillsFuture credit top-up of $500 scheme for adult Singaporeans aged 25 and above and the special SkillsFuture credit top-up scheme for Singaporeans aged 40 to 60.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For those who have utilised the SkillsFuture Credit, what percentage has actually resulted in successful career switches or career progression?

sections.label: MediFund applicant abuse prevention
sections.summary: Asks what prevents a MediFund applicant from seeking extra supplies at different institutions or waiving medical record sharing under PDPA rights.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, what is in place to prevent a MediFund applicant from going to different healthcare institutions seeking more-than-required medical supplies, nutritional supplements and medications?

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the applicant ask for waiver from the National Electronic Medical Record sharing, quoting PDPA rights, to avoid detection?

sections.label: S Pass flexibility for employers
sections.summary: The speaker appeals for MOM to show flexibility to employers who tried hiring locally before turning to foreign workers, instead of a blanket S Pass limit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Irene Quay Siew Ching (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, instead of a blanket policy to limit S Passes with minimal exceptions, I would still like to appeal for MOM to consider showing flexibility to employers trying to hire locally with failed attempts to turn to foreign workers.

sections.label: Manpower-lean approach beyond automation
sections.summary: The speaker says Singapore has gone beyond simply automating things, taking a more sophisticated approach to becoming manpower-lean in services.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Can I provide a quick response to Ms Irene Quay?

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I understand where the Member is coming from, but can I just say that at today's stage of development for Singapore, especially when it comes to seeking productivity improvements and finding manpower savings in the services sector, we have gone far beyond the idea of simply automating things.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: It is a much more sophisticated approach towards becoming more manpower-lean.

sections.label: Noodle portioning business opportunity
sections.summary: A noodle maker found a business opportunity in F&B outlets where two staff spend two hours daily portioning three-kilogramme noodle packs into 150-gram portions.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They make hokkien noodles that we eat, they make kuay teow that we also eat.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, I asked them, "Where are you finding business opportunities?" And they told me that one of the things that they discovered was that in F&B outlets, quite often, two staff spend two hours everyday doing one thing: portioning out noodles that were delivered to the outlet in three-kilogramme packs into smaller portions of 150 grams.

sections.label: Machine replacing noodle portioning work
sections.summary: Two workers spend two hours portioning noodles, which the noodle maker said a machine can do, addressing outlet manpower constraints.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: They get two workers standing there – maybe around 10 o'clock, nine o'clock – and for two hours, they do nothing but portioning out the noodles.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, he said, "This is a business opportunity for me." The outlet has got a lot of manpower constraints, but actually this portioning can be done by the machine.

sections.label: Stocktaking and customer indifference
sections.summary: The passage states that the customer does not care about taking stock or taking note of inventory.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Stocktaking	– the customer does not care about you taking stock, taking note of inventory.

sections.label: Budget help and support measures
sections.summary: This Budget provides help and support to industries, businessmen and affected people to ease financial burden and build financial resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In this Budget, measures are taken so that the industries, businessmen and those affected by the current situation are given help and support to mitigate their financial burden and, at the same time, help to maintain financial resilience in an increasingly gloomy economic outlook.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Help and support are also provided for those affected in society so that they can rise up and rebuild their financial capabilities during the recovery phase.

sections.label: Healthcare workers honoured as heroes
sections.summary: Healthcare workers were honoured as heroes for carrying on their duties despite facing possible infection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Healthcare workers like doctors, nurses, paramedics and other healthcare officers were honoured as heroes for carrying on with their duties sincerely and diligently even though they face the possibility of getting infected.

sections.label: Cynicism and panic buying criticism
sections.summary: Social media posts showed healthcare workers receiving cynical comments, and panic buying drew rebukes, which the passage says weakens psychological resilience and social unity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Several posts shared on social media channels showed incidents where healthcare workers received cynical comments and were treated poorly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is an unhealthy situation and it must stop.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This incident caused many people to make comments that rebuke and criticise, that described those who took part in panic buying as people who only think of themselves and as kiasu people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some felt that panic buying was a reaction to a previous situation, where the stocks of masks and hand sanitisers were depleted despite assurances by the Government that there are enough supplies of masks and asked Singaporeans not to worry.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Accusations and finger-pointing are unwarranted and may further aggravate the anxiety that was already there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These kinds of negative actions like condemnations, criticisms and finger-pointing will weaken psychological resilience and have an unhealthy impact on social unity.

sections.label: Avoiding finger-pointing, advising one another
sections.summary: The passage urges avoiding finger-pointing and encourages advising one another to strengthen psychological resilience and social and national unity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Avoid any finger-pointing because, as the saying goes, 'When you point one finger at others, the rest of your fingers are pointing at yourself." Sir, it is true that the practice of advising one another, reminding others to be good and patient with others, is a good practice that should be encouraged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This practice is a constructive effort that should be done at all levels of society in order to inculcate, preserve and strengthen psychological resilience so that social and national unity will not be shaken or become tainted during challenging times.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This year's Budget is, indeed, generous, particularly with the Stabilisation and Support Package, which helps to mitigate current economic challenges, partly fueled by the COVID-19 public health situation.

sections.label: SkillsFuture and mid-career support
sections.summary: The passage lauds the Next Bound of SkillsFuture, the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package and the SkillsFuture Credit Top-up giving $1,000 per person.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government has done well in this and there are many initiatives, programmes and policies that have been revised and implemented to cater to this.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I am heartened by the The Next Bound of SkillsFuture announced in this year's Budget, which will help provide Singaporeans with opportunities to develop to their fullest potential throughout life and not only when they are young.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I laud the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package and the SkillsFuture Credit Top-up for Singaporeans in their 40s and 50s, which, essentially, means they get a total of $1,000 per person.

sections.label: Grants for older workers
sections.summary: The passage lauds the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and Part-time Re-employment Grant that help employers review hiring policies to keep older workers employed.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: (In English): I also laud the Senior Worker Early Adopter Grant and the Part-time Re-employment Grant that will help companies and employers review their hiring policies to help older workers stay employed.

sections.label: Employers and disability employment grants
sections.summary: Few employers are willing to employ persons with disabilities or special needs despite Government-funded employment grants such as the Special Employment Credit, Workfare Training Scheme and Open Door Programme.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Not many employers are willing to employ persons with disabilities or special needs even though there are Government-funded employment grants to facilitate this, such as the Special Employment Credit, Workfare Training Scheme and the Open Door Programme.

sections.label: Inclusion of persons with disabilities
sections.summary: Improvements have been made towards inclusion, but more is needed for persons with disabilities or special needs to be financially independent, recognised and part of community, society, schools and workplaces.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While there have been improvements made to making our society and workplaces more inclusive towards persons with disabilities or special needs, there is still a long way to go in ensuring they can be financially independent, recognised for their abilities and talents and not be judged for being atypical and that they can very much be a part of our community, society, schools and workplaces as every one else.

sections.label: Flexi-work provisions rolled out
sections.summary: Flexi-work provisions, arrangement and support have been extensively rolled out during this period.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Flexi-work provisions, arrangement and support have been extensively rolled out during this period.

sections.label: FWAs for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: FWAs can give persons with disabilities or special needs better employment opportunities, and employers are urged to carry on with them during the COVID-19 public health situation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In addition, as I have mentioned in my Budget speech last year, FWAs can provide for better employment opportunities for persons with disabilities or special needs to work from home or to gradually adjust to their work environments and work commitments at a pace they are comfortable with.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Being gainfully employed and being able to be remunerated for doing meaningful work is a start in helping persons with disabilities or special needs live independently like many others and it accords suﬃcient opportunities to develop that much-needed self-belief and self-dignity.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Hence, I urge employers and companies to carry on with their FWAs that we already have in place now during the current COVID-19 public health situation so that our society, communities and workplaces can be a lot more inclusive, especially for those who are less privileged or who face more challenges in life.

sections.label: Lifetime prevalence of mental illness
sections.summary: Lifetime prevalence of mental illness in Singapore rose from 10% or more in 1998 and 2007 to 12% in 2010 and now 13.9%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As a nation, we clearly struggle with mental health.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There has been a steady increase in the lifetime prevalence of mental illness in Singapore over two decades – 10% or more when it was first tracked in 1998 and 2007, to 12% in 2010 and now 13.9%.

sections.label: Mental health healthcare expenditure
sections.summary: The Health Minister shared that only 3% of healthcare operating expenditure in FY2017 went to mental health, compared to 11% for diabetes, and FY2020 estimates have only three mental health items.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In fact, the Health Minister has previously shared in this House that we only spent 3% of our healthcare operating expenditure in FY2017 on mental health, compared to 11% for diabetes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under our FY2020 expenditure estimates for healthcare, there are only three expenditure items targeted to support mental health.

sections.label: Mental healthcare costs survey
sections.summary: Sixty-six percent of respondents said mental healthcare costs were high, over half of them public healthcare users.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Sixty-six percent of the respondents shared that mental healthcare costs were high, with more than half of them being users of public healthcare services.

sections.label: MediSave, community organisations, psychiatrist numbers
sections.summary: MediSave should be allowed at Government or quasi-Government-funded community organisations, with about 248 psychiatrists and 473 psychologists practising in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MediSave should also be allowed for services at Government or quasi-Government-funded community organisations, because how can we have a community health approach if it is not?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are around 248 psychiatrists and 473 psychologists practising in Singapore, or 4.4 psychiatrists and 8.3 psychologists per 100,000 population which may explain why the overall median waiting time for new subsidised appointments across the public hospitals is 27 days to see a psychiatrist and 28 days to see a psychologist .

sections.label: CHAT mental health check service
sections.summary: CHAT offers free confidential mental health checks keeping data out of the public health system, plus care navigation with subsidised referral.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: CHAT provides a unique combination of: one, free and confidential mental health check service that guarantees data will not be entered into the public health system; and two, care navigation that includes subsidised referral for public mental healthcare services if required.

sections.label: Dissatisfaction with public mental healthcare
sections.summary: Over 50 respondents were gravely dissatisfied with public mental healthcare quality; 36 percent cited lack of empathy and dismal psychiatric wards.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: More than 50 respondents, however, indicated grave dissatisfaction with the quality of public mental healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirty-six percent explicitly mentioned lack of empathy in the professionals they interacted with and the dismal environment of psychiatric wards in our public hospitals.

sections.label: Conversations beyond youths, patient ages
sections.summary: Conversations must move beyond youths, since average age of subsidised patients for mental health conditions was 40 to 50 in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Yet, to truly facilitate an SG Together response, we need such conversations to move beyond only the youths, especially since the average age of subsidised patients for the different mental health conditions was between 40 to 50 years old in the last three years.

sections.label: Rising childhood mental distress, SOS calls
sections.summary: Calls by five- to nine-year-olds to the Samaritans of Singapore jumped 500 percent over a three-year period.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Would we then start to ask what are the causes of rising levels of mental distress in childhood that saw calls made by five- to nine-year-olds to the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) jumped by 500% over a three-year period?

sections.label: Mental health as budget priority
sections.summary: A Member asks the Deputy Prime Minister what must happen for mental health to become a national and budget priority, and urges preventive action.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Already, a late 2019 study found that stress-related illnesses cost Singapore's economy $3.2 billion annually.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I would like to earnestly ask the Deputy Prime Minister what needs to happen for mental health to be a national and budget priority?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Do we have to wait for one in four Singaporeans with mental health conditions, like the current global average, for us to take urgent action?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can we afford negative growth in productivity and innovation before realising how mental well-being is intricately tied to human performance?

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, I wish to conclude by imploring the Government to take action now to make quality mental healthcare accessible and affordable for all Singaporeans, to bring this on par to the world-class public healthcare system for all that we are proud of.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, I challenge the Government to boldly take a strategic and preventive approach to deliver mental well-being and total health to our people as it has done spectacularly with economic well-being, so that we can bring and build the social resilience and psychological capital to thrive as a nation and flourish as human beings.

sections.label: COVID-19 and Budget 2020
sections.summary: COVID-19 hit the economy and way of life, and Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat's team produced Budget 2020 to support businesses, workers and families.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop, COVID-19 came along and slammed our economy and our way of life and threatened to bring us into a recession.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: To help us overcome these challenges, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat and his team have put together a very generous Budget 2020 with a wide-ranging package of measures to support and sustain businesses, workers and families in the short term.

sections.label: Seniors in Budget 2020
sections.summary: The Budget gives seniors more Silver Support Scheme beneficiaries, higher payouts and dollar-for-dollar matching for family CPF top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: A wealthier Government today is showing their appreciation with generous packages and top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Therefore, I am especially happy that our seniors have been given special attention in this Budget: more Silver Support Scheme beneficiaries, higher payouts and dollar-for-dollar matching when their families top up their CPF accounts.

sections.label: Harvard praise for COVID-19 detection
sections.summary: Researchers of a Harvard University study said Singapore set the gold standard for COVID-19 detection around the world.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The researchers of a Harvard University study said, "Singapore set the gold standard for COVID-19 detection around the world”.

sections.label: Food drive after DORSCON Orange
sections.summary: Two days after DORSCON went to Orange and amid panic buying reports, volunteers continued their monthly food donation drive for needy residents.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Just two days after the raising of the DORSCON alert to Orange, and amidst reports of panic buying at supermarkets island-wide, our volunteers continued their monthly food donation drive to help needy residents.

sections.label: Neighbours help infected family
sections.summary: A Member saw neighbours rally around an infected family, notes some may be overwhelmed by information, and supports the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: While I sensed some residents had uneasiness and questions about the virus outbreak, I was especially heartened when I witnessed neighbours rallying around the infected family.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: One neighbour offered to buy the family their daily necessities while another offered to deliver meals.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: Some people, such as our seniors and smaller enterprises, may be overwhelmed by all the information.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: I am optimistic that this Budget will resonate with Singaporeans and set us on a firm footing for our continuous nation-building journey.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: On this note, Sir, I support this Budget.

sections.label: Elderly support ratio halving
sections.summary: The ratio of younger persons to an elderly person was 10.5 in 1990 and halved to 4.5 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 1990, it was 10.5 younger persons to an elderly person.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2019, the ratio has halved to 4.5.

sections.label: Caregivers for elderly survey
sections.summary: A 2011 national survey found 97.9% of informal caregivers in Singapore are immediate family members, mostly female and aged 45 to 59.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A 2011 national survey on caregiving for elderly individuals, those above 75 years old requiring help with at least one activity of daily living found that 97.9% of all informal caregivers in Singapore are immediate family members, with more of them being female and between 45 and 59 years old.

sections.label: Women outside labour force caregiving
sections.summary: In 2018, over 280,000 women were outside the labour force mainly because of caregiving to relatives or family members apart from children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, over 280,000 women were outside the labour force primarily because of caregiving to relatives or family members apart from children.

sections.label: Female caregivers income loss
sections.summary: A recent study shows female family caregivers to older persons suffered a 63% average income loss, an average annual loss of more than $50,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Similarly, a recent study shows that female family caregivers to older persons experienced a change in work situation because of caregiving, suffering a 63% loss in income on average, which translated into an average annual loss of more than $50,000.

sections.label: Paid family care leave, care costs
sections.summary: In 2018, only 20% of companies offered paid family care leave, and a local study found lower- and middle-income households would spend 23% to 59% of household income on long-term care after subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, only 20% of companies offered some type of paid family care leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a local study, they found that lower- and middle-income households would spend between 23% and 59% of their household income on long-term care services after subsidies.

sections.label: Sexual misconduct at universities
sections.summary: From Academic Year 2015/2016 to 2017/2018, 56 sexual misconduct cases were reported to autonomous universities in Singapore, 37 of them to the Police.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From the Academic Year 2015/2016 to 2017/2018, 56 cases of sexual misconduct were reported to autonomous universities in Singapore and 37 of these cases were reported to the Police.

sections.label: National code on campus sexual violence
sections.summary: Violence should be treated the same regardless of setting, so a national code on campus sexual violence for all education institutions is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Violence is violence, and should be dealt with in the same way, regardless of institutional setting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, I believe the way forward is for the development of a national code or guideline addressing campus sexual violence that all education institutions can adopt.

sections.label: Technology-facilitated sexual violence cases rising
sections.summary: AWARE saw technology-facilitated sexual violence cases rise threefold in three years, with 124 cases in 2018, and effects can be as traumatic as other sexual violence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the Association of Women for Action and Research (AWARE), the number of technology-facilitated sexual violence cases they have seen had increased threefold in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, they saw 124 cases, more than half of which involved sexual images of the survivors that were non-consensually shared, obtained or created.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The effects of technology-facilitated sexual violence on the survivor can be just as traumatic as other forms of sexual violence.

sections.label: Swift removal of intimate materials
sections.summary: Mechanisms could allow swift removal of non-consensually shared intimate materials, with the Commissioner empowered to issue 48-hour removal notices, and a similar mechanism should be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps mechanisms could be set up for the swift removal of non-consensually shared intimate materials, even before conviction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Commissioner is then empowered to issue removal notices for the end-user or service provider to remove the materials in question within 48 hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yip Pin Xiu (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should consider having such a similar mechanism in place.

sections.label: Reviewing childcare leave provisions
sections.summary: Childcare leave provides time for working parents to care for children, but provisions have not been increased for over a decade and should be reviewed again.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad we provide childcare leave, which "will provide sufficient time for working parents to care for and spend quality time with their children".

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But it has been more than a decade since childcare leave provisions were increased and it is time to review this again.

sections.label: HFMD infection rate by age 12
sections.summary: In Singapore, 90% of children have had HFMD infection by 12 years of age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In Singapore, 90% of children have had HFMD infection by 12 years of age.

sections.label: Benefits of childcare sick leave
sections.summary: Childcare sick leave will help children, parents and ultimately employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Having childcare sick leave will help the children, the parents and, ultimately, the employers.

sections.label: Public Service childcare sick leave
sections.summary: The Public Service, a large Singapore employer, already gives some officers childcare sick leave on a per-child basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The Public Service, one of the largest employers in Singapore, already gives some officers childcare sick leave and it is on a per-child basis.

sections.label: Parents' time with children
sections.summary: Many people say that leaving kids at childcare most of the time raises the question of why have kids, so parents need more time with children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But many I spoke to feel that if they are going to have kids but just leave them at childcare centres most of the time, then what is the point of having kids?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are trying hard to increase our total fertility rate (TFR) and, beyond looking at the dollars and cents, we also need to look into providing parents with more time to spend with their children.

sections.label: Private sector leave benefits
sections.summary: In 2018, 20% of private sector companies offered such leave benefits, up from 15% in 2012.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In 2018, 20% of private sector companies offered such leave benefits, up from 15% in 2012.

sections.label: Parent-care leave for everyone
sections.summary: Eight years after parent-care leave began in the Civil Service, it is time for everyone else to have it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Spend time with those you love and remember that life is a one-way ticket.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It has been eight years since we introduced parent-care leave in the Civil Service and it is now time for everyone else to have this.

sections.label: Family-friendly employer and Government
sections.summary: The speaker says they are a family-friendly employer and should be a family-friendly Government, and asks why civil servants get paid parent-care leave while others get unpaid leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We are a family-friendly employer and now we should be a family-friendly Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand that the tripartite partners have also encouraged more employers to adopt the Tripartite Standard on Unpaid Leave for Unexpected Care Needs, regardless of whether they already provide parent-care leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Why do civil servants get paid parent-care leave and others have unpaid leave?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I also understand that caregivers have given feedback that they prefer FWAs over parental leave as a more sustainable way to balance work and caregiving responsibilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But the parent-care leave we provide to everyone can, again, be the same as those provided to civil servants where they have the flexibility to take this leave in full or half-day blocks.

sections.label: Singapore heating and temperatures
sections.summary: The island is heating up twice as fast as the world, and maximum temperatures could reach 35°C to 37°C by 2100.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our island is now being heated up twice as fast compared to the world, and maximum temperatures, we are told, could reach 35°C to 37°C by the year 2100.

sections.label: Sea level rise and fund
sections.summary: Thirty percent of Singapore's land lies under five metres above sea level, and sea level could rise about half a metre by 2100, so a $5 billion Coastal and Flood Protection Fund is timely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirty percent of Singapore's land area lies less than five metres above mean sea level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Even under an optimistic emissions scenario, there has been projected that sea level in Singapore could rise by about half a metre by 2100, posing a coastal flood risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, the establishment of the new Coastal and Flood Protection Fund with an initial injection of $5 billion is a timely move.

sections.label: Phasing out ICE vehicles
sections.summary: The Workers' Party welcomes the Government phasing out all internal combustion engine vehicles by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party, therefore, welcomes the Government phasing out all internal combustion engine (ICE) vehicles by 2040.

sections.label: Power mix and charging points
sections.summary: The passage asks how the carbon footprint of power generation will be lowered from 2030 to 2040, and notes 28,000 charging points by 2030 may mean one per 10 EVs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While our current power generation mix will improve by 2030 due to more solar capacity, how are we moving to lowering the carbon footprint of our power generation in 2030 to 2040?

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Also, with regard to charging points, the Government expects to have 28,000 charging points by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: But even assuming a 30% conversion from the current vehicle population to EVs, it still means about one charging point to 10 EVs by 2030.

sections.label: Households' share of electricity
sections.summary: These households make up around 21% of total resident households but accounted for 41.4% of total electricity consumed in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Even as they make up around 21% of the total resident households in Singapore, they account for 41.4% of the total electricity consumed in 2018.

sections.label: Land use and nature reserves
sections.summary: An NParks study indicated Singapore's land became a net carbon emitter in 2014, and the passage asks whether the Government will commit to securing nature reserves and protecting green ecosystems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Already, a National Parks Board (NParks) study indicated that Singapore's land became a net carbon emitter in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Over the past few years, we have seen the prioritisation of development projects over the benefits afforded by sensitive ecosystems due to such projects as the Cross Island Line, the Tengah HDB project and the Mandai Project.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thankfully, environmental groups, academics and public agencies have come together seeking to reduce the negative impacts these projects will have on the environment, in particular on our local biodiversity and forest cover, even after mitigation measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: However, the question remains whether the Government will commit to securing the inviolability of our nature reserves and greater protection of the little that is left of our more natural, green ecosystems in the future, while finding better ways to plan land use for housing, transport and tourism.

sections.label: Climate facts and Green Agenda
sections.summary: The National Climate Change Secretariat should consider working with research agencies and researchers so easy-to-access climate facts are public, and a bold Green Agenda should be considered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As the lead Government agency on climate change, the National Climate Change Secretariat should consider working with public and private research agencies and researchers on this so that easy-to-access facts and evidence on climate change can be in the public domain to build further buy-in for green policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As such, a bold Green Agenda should be considered as Singapore moves to the next chapter of nation-building.

sections.label: Singapore per capita income growth
sections.summary: Singapore's per capita income rose from about S$1,600 in 1965 to about S$90,000 in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Singapore's per capita income was about S$1,600 when we became independent in 1965 – just S$1,600.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Today, in 2019, our per capita income is about S$90,000.

sections.label: Healthcare costs and GST increase
sections.summary: Healthcare spending is budgeted at S$13.4 billion, up 16%, prompting a recommended GST increase of two percentage points between 2022 and 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Singapore’s healthcare expenditure is budgeted at S$13.4 billion for this year's Budget and that is an increase of 16% just from last year's Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: This means that we have to address such increase in healthcare costs soon if we do not want to kick the can down the road for a future government to deal with and, to do so, in a way, by using recurring revenue because rising healthcare costs is a recurring expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Therefore, the Finance Minister has recommended a Goods and Services Tax (GST) rate increase of two percentage points to take place between 2022 and 2025.

sections.label: NIRC in 2020 Budget
sections.summary: NIRC is expected to be S$17 billion in the 2020 Budget, lower than S$19 billion in FY2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, NIRC is expected to be S$17 billion in our 2020 Budget, but lower than the S$19 billion in FY2019.

sections.label: Long-term planning and climate change
sections.summary: Singapore is putting aside S$5 billion to address rising sea levels and climate change.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Today, our tree-lined roads, our air and sea ports and our skyline are the envy of many.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: We are continuing with such long-term planning and are putting aside S$5 billion now to address rising sea levels and climate change.

sections.label: Budget deficit, surplus and packages
sections.summary: The Budget sets aside $4 billion for COVID-19 challenges, expects a $10.9 billion deficit, and has a S$7.7 billion surplus for this term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I have also talked about adopting a long-term planning horizon when it comes to Government budgeting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: But beyond these issues, this year’s Budget has also set aside an additional $4 billion to address short-term immediate challenges like cushioning the impact of the COVID-19 outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Although we do expect an overall Budget deficit of $10.9 billion for 2020, there is still a S$7.7 billion surplus for this term of Government commencing from 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Therefore, all the capital and operating expenditures as well as Government transfers, including the transfers into the Merdeka Generation (MG) package, are all earned by the respective terms of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In fact, the total recurring cost of the Merdeka Generation package as well as the Pioneer Generation package are all paid for upfront and all earned by the respective terms of Government.

sections.label: Stability and Support Package sectors
sections.summary: The Stability and Support Package helps Tourism, Aviation, Retail, F&B and Point-to-Point transport, with tax and rental rebates, wage support and training incentives.
