sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The Government has come up with the Stability and Support Package to help key sectors of the economy – Tourism, Aviation, Retail, Food and Beverage (F&B), and Point-to-Point transport services – that are hit hardest by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am encouraged that the Budget will cater for tax and rental rebates to defray the cost of businesses, as well as wage-support schemes and training incentives to upskill Singaporeans and keep Singaporeans employed during these difficult times.

sections.label: Early childhood and after-school care support
sections.summary: The Government committed $1 billion to early childhood in 2018, raised KiFAS income eligibility to $12,000 a month, and will set up a $350 million Community Capability Trust.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2018, the Government committed $1 billion to the early childhood sector and I understand that it will invest almost twice this amount per year for the next few years to further support this sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While we have raised the income eligibility for additional subsidies for the Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme (KiFAS) to $12,000 a month to benefit a larger number of families, would the Government consider putting in place more support and subsidy for after-school student care once the child graduates from preschool and enters primary school?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe this will help support families, especially by providing working parents alternative care arrangements for children, while they are at work It was announced in the Budget that over the next 10 years, the Government will also set up a Community Capability Trust of up to $350 million to support our Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to strengthen their organisational capabilities and enhance their levels of service provision.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit for differently-abled
sections.summary: The Enabling Employment Credit will replace existing schemes to support employment of differently-abled individuals by providing wage offsets for employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As announced in the Budget, the Enabling Employment Credit (EEC) will replace existing schemes to support the employment of differently-abled individuals by providing wage offsets for employers.

sections.label: Budget for COVID-19 economic uncertainties
sections.summary: This Budget helps Singapore get through COVID-19 economic uncertainties and shows the Government's decisiveness and commitment to Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: More importantly, this is a Budget to help Singapore get through the economic uncertainties during COVID-19 and to ensure that we emerge stronger from this entire episode.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The current Budget demonstrates the decisiveness of the Government and its commitment to Singapore and Singaporeans as it has acted quickly and decisively to come up with a budget to deal with the many challenges that have arisen due to COVID-19.

sections.label: Enabling Employment Credit for PwDs
sections.summary: The Government introduced the EEC to support employers of PwDs, helping PwDs find employment and remain in the workforce, signalling inclusivity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am always keen to see the initiatives in the Budget that will help shape our values as a people.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: This year, the Government introduced the EEC to provide stronger support for employers of PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The intent is to provide help for PwDs to find employment and remain in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: To me, this is important as it is a signal to be inclusive and normalise PwDs' participation in our society.

sections.label: Lack of awareness of support
sections.summary: There is still a lack of awareness of the different types of support available for families with children with different needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Through this experience, we have found that: firstly, there is still a lack of awareness of the different types of support available for families with children with different needs.

sections.label: Culture of care for PwDs
sections.summary: Feedback from parents and family members repeatedly raised the need to build a culture of care and compassion towards PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: More significantly, one theme that repeatedly comes up from the feedback from parents and family members is the need to build a culture of care and compassion towards PwDs.

sections.label: Youth support and mentoring programmes
sections.summary: The passage describes support for youths through the National Youth Fund, SG Youth Action Plan, Young Changemakers Programme, overseas exposure, M3 mentoring, and online resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Now more than ever, young people are given opportunities and are empowered to make the change they want to see.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There are many support mechanisms, for example, through the National Youth Fund, the SG Youth Action Plan and NYC's Young Changemakers Programme, which not only provide monetary grants but connect youths with mentors and like-minded peers to help implement ground-up projects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: Aside from providing support to youths for their causes and to carry out their projects, it is also important to support them to achieve their aspirations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I note the provision in the Budget to ready our youths for various opportunities by providing more overseas exposure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We should also continue to build on the efforts to support youths through empowerment and mentoring programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I oversee the youth engagement efforts under M3 and one of the key initiatives is to create a culture of mentoring within the community so that the Malay/Muslim youths have somewhere to turn to for guidance as they navigate through challenges and choices in life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There are also resources like the MENDAKI Future-Ready Toolkit and the M3 Resource Directory which are available online for youths to refer to for information on various matters.

sections.label: Involving youths in policy discussion
sections.summary: The passage states young people should be involved in discussing key issues and policies, with budget and platforms provided for their ideas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: We should involve young people in discussion of key issues and policies and find opportunities to work with them to create positive social norms within the community.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There should, therefore, be an appropriate budget allocated for these efforts as well as provision of the necessary platforms for them to implement their ideas and work with people from different ages and backgrounds.

sections.label: MTI projected growth rate
sections.summary: The Ministry of Trade and Industry reduced its projected growth rate to a lower range of -0.5% to 1.5% for 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) reduced its projected growth rate to a lower range of -0.5% to 1.5% for 2020.

sections.label: Care and Support Package
sections.summary: The passage states many Singaporeans are happy with the $1.6 billion Care and Support Package because it puts money directly into their pockets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Individually, many Singaporeans are happy with the Care and Support Package of $1.6 billion because it puts money directly into their pockets.

sections.label: Schemes helping businesses retain staff
sections.summary: The passage states most workers prefer not to be on welfare, and the Jobs Support Scheme, Wage Credit Scheme, corporate tax rebate and rental waivers help businesses retain staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Most workers prefer not to be on any form of welfare.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Hence, the Jobs Support Scheme (JSS), the Wage Credit Scheme, the corporate tax rebate and the rental waivers for some of the tenants would help businesses to survive the economic slowdown and allow them to retain their staff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I am also pleased that the Finance Minister had remembered the hawkers in the food centres and markets.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit usage question
sections.summary: The passage appreciates government intent to help Singaporeans stay employable and asks how many have not used the 2016 SkillsFuture Credit of $500.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Next, I appreciate the intent of the Government to help Singaporeans stay employable and to use the SkillsFuture Credit to learn new skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: However, may I ask the Finance Minister how many Singaporeans have not used the 2016 SkillsFuture Credit of $500?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit and Budget expenditure
sections.summary: The 2016 and 2020 SkillsFuture Credit may remain untouched for a long time, and it is now the second largest Budget expenditure, just before Defence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Otherwise, the 2016 and now the 2020 SkillsFuture Credit may remain untouched for a long period of time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It now accounts for the second largest expenditure of the Government's Budget, just before Defence.

sections.label: Budget, GST and healthcare spending
sections.summary: The speaker says healthcare costs will rise, urges outreach on GST offset packages, and calls the Budget good, bold and responsive, with a $10.9 billion deficit and $7.8 billion war chest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Although the Minister has assured us that the GST hike will not take place next year, the reality is that healthcare costs will continue to rise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Government needs to decide how to apportion the taxes which is collected and what resources to allocate into Healthcare, compared to Defence, Education, Housing and Transport.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But Singaporeans must understand that increased spending on healthcare must come from somewhere.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to reach out to more Singaporeans to help them learn about the GST offset packages which are intended to help the lower-income cope with the GST eventual increase.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Overall, I am of the view that this is a good Budget to take care of affected Singaporeans and to prepare the country for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It shows that the Government deeply cares for its citizens and the deferment of the GST increase is a clear signal that the Government is responsive to feedback from the citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This is a big, bold Budget which comes at the price of a $10.9 billion deficit, responding to the need for help by Singaporean households and businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: With an accumulated surplus of $18.7 billion over this current term of office, there remains a war chest of $7.8 billion, which is very reassuring.

sections.label: Care and Support Package relief
sections.summary: The Government's Care and Support Package will provide some relief to individuals whose income was disrupted by COVID-19's impact on businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Government's Care and Support Package will go some way to provide relief to individuals who have experienced income disruptions due to the impact of COVID-19 on businesses.

sections.label: JSS cash grant for employers
sections.summary: Under JSS, employers will receive an 8% cash grant on the wages of local employees for October to December 2019.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under JSS, employers will receive the 8% cash grant on the wages of local employees for the months of October to December 2019.

sections.label: Rent rebates called insufficient
sections.summary: Businesses said the one-month rent rebates for NEA hawker centres and markets and half-month for commercial tenants in Government-managed properties are insufficient, expecting normalcy only by the second half of the year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Feedback from various businesses indicated that the rent rebates of one month for National Environment Agency (NEA) hawker centres and markets, and half month for commercial tenants in Government-managed properties are insufficient as they expect that the situation will take at least till the second half of the year before it returns to normal.

sections.label: SkillsFuture courses and industry cooperation
sections.summary: The speaker suggests tax incentives for telecommunications or selected sectors, closer MOM and IHL cooperation on SkillsFuture course quality, constant review of course materials and instructors, and mobile modular sections for accreditation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps tax incentives for the telecommunications or selected sectors can be provided so that they can lower the fees for the ecosystem to promote adoption and switchovers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Closer cooperation between MOM and institutes of higher learning (IHLs) will be necessary to ensure that the SkillsFuture courses are of high quality and are relevant to industry to support our economy’s transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The course materials, modes of instruction, quality of instructors, just to name a few, should be constantly reviewed and audited to ensure that they are up to par.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The courses could also be broken down into mobile modular sections for the workers to learn on the go and achieve accreditation over time.

sections.label: COVID-19 support packages and forecasts
sections.summary: The Stabilisation and Support Package and Care and Support Package are compared with the 2003 SARS package, alongside downgraded growth forecasts and S&P 500 losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The $5.6 billion Stabilisation and Support Package, even if adjusted for inflation, far outstrips the $230 million SARS package in 2003.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The $1.6 billion Care and Support Package not only provides a leg up but also goes towards, hopefully, stimulating the economy through spending.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: MTI has downgraded the 2020 economic growth forecast, projected between -0.5% and 1.5% on the impact of COVID-19, just slightly better than Hong Kong’s projected -1.5% to 0.5%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: According to Standard and Poor's (S&P) Dow Jones, the S&P 500 has wiped out $2.138 trillion since last Wednesday with $1.737 trillion or 63% loss in two days of trade since the start of the week.

sections.label: Responsible overall Budget deficit
sections.summary: The passage states a need to be responsive and responsible, and expects an overall Budget deficit of $10.95 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: While we need to be responsive, we also need to be responsible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: We expect to run an overall Budget deficit of $10.95 billion.

sections.label: Credit to DPM and MOF
sections.summary: Credit is given to the Deputy Prime Minister, the Ministry of Finance team and other Ministries for responding rapidly to the crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Credit is due to the Deputy Prime Minister and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) team as well as the other Ministries for being able to respond to this crisis so rapidly.

sections.label: Remarkable for responsive and responsible
sections.summary: The passage states it is remarkable because it is responsive and also remains responsible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, remarkable because it is responsive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is also remarkable because it remains responsible.

sections.label: Residents baked cookies together
sections.summary: A total of 136 residents came together and baked close to 11,000 cookies that day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: A total of 136 residents came together and we baked close to 11,000 cookies that day.

sections.label: Recognising frontline workers with dignity
sections.summary: The speaker asks that frontline workers be given back their dignity and that Singaporeans earn forgiveness for shunning them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: With love, respect and to the best of my ability because, just like the Nurse's Pledge I took, I will uphold my integrity.” Mr Speaker, when this crisis comes to pass, when we get back to normalcy, I ask that we commit ourselves to doing something meaningful to recognise our frontline workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Give them back the dignity they deserve and, in the process, earn on behalf of all Singaporeans the forgiveness we all need for shunning them.

sections.label: SMEs and landlord savings
sections.summary: Asks how much of the $4 billion assistance will help SMEs and how landlords will be made to share savings with them.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Of the $4 billion assistance, how much will be used to help SMEs?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How can we make sure that landlords will share the savings with the SMEs?

sections.label: Grab and Gojek driver support
sections.summary: Relays feedback that some Grab and Gojek drivers are ineligible for the full-time driver support package due to fewer trips from reduced demand.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In Malay):   I have also received feedback from several Grab and Gojek drivers who said that they are not eligible for the support package for full-time drivers, because they do not meet the minimum number of trips made due to reduced demand within that period, Will the Minister be able to take a look at this group?

sections.label: Jurong Regional Line contracts
sections.summary: States that in the LTA Jurong Regional Line Projects, four of seven contracts went to foreign contractors.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In the Land Transport Authority (LTA) Jurong Regional Line Projects, for example, four out of seven contracts were awarded to foreign contractors.

sections.label: Paying foreign contractor more
sections.summary: Asks why $6 million more is paid to a foreign contractor.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Why pay $6 million more to a foreign contractor?

sections.label: Traffic noise enforcement examples
sections.summary: Cites a 2009 Swedish report on traffic noise and heart attacks, plus UK, Calgary and Abu Dhabi noise enforcement measures.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: If I may refer to a Swedish report published in 2009, which found people who were regularly exposed to traffic noise in excess of 50 decibels were 40% more likely to suffer a heart attack than those who lived in quieter neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The UK use Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) tech to dish out fines to drivers over excessive noise.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Calgary, a city in Canada, is using Sound Camera and fines motorists with excessively loud vehicles.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Similarly, Abu Dhabi Police have invented a noise-measuring camera which will help officers take action against abnormally loud cars.

sections.label: Town Councils online procurement request
sections.summary: States that some Town Councils have asked HDB since January 2018 to let them procure goods and services online.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Another example, some Town Councils have been asking the HDB since January 2018 to allow Town Councils to procure our goods and services online.

sections.label: Support for the Budget
sections.summary: The speaker says he does not want to empty the House, quotes a song lyric to the Deputy Prime Minister, and states he supports the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: And I do not want to empty this House.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: But I will say this to the Deputy Prime Minister: "Walk on, walk on With hope in your heart And you'll never walk alone You'll never walk alone." Mr Speaker, Sir, I support the Budget.

sections.label: Our Singapore Fund top-up
sections.summary: Heng Swee Keat said the Government will set aside $250 million for community partnership projects, including $20 million to top up the Our Singapore Fund, extended five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For instance, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat shared that the Government will set aside $250 million to boost efforts to partner the community in projects during the recent Budget announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This includes the $20 million that will be used to top up the Our Singapore Fund (OSF), which supports projects in the social and community domains initiated by citizens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Fund will also be extended for five more years from this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since OSF was announced in Budget 2016, I understand that it has committed nearly $4.3 million to more than 240 ground-up projects in areas ranging from heritage to sports.

sections.label: Matching for earned income
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the Ministry consider matching not only funds raised but also earned income such as ticket proceeds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps, the Ministry can consider matching not only for funds raised, but also for earned income, such as the ticket proceeds.

sections.label: CMF flexibility for arts groups
sections.summary: The speaker notes the $20 million OSF top-up and $250 million for community partnerships, and asks for more flexible, targeted CMF administration, including matching ticket sales.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the Budget Statement announced recently, Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat shared that the Government will set aside $20 million to top up OSF and extend the fund to 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Government will set aside $250 million to boost efforts involving community partnerships, with $20 million earmarked for OSF top-ups to encourage more ground-up community initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The sustained development of arts groups is not only dependent on strong Government support, but also the support of companies and foundations that identify with them, as well as the active participation, sponsorship and donation of our people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government will consider exercising greater flexibility and adopt a more targeted approach in the administration of CMF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, besides providing matching funds for donations, the Government could perhaps consider providing matching funds based on proceeds from performances and ticket sales.

sentences.speaker: Mr Terence Ho Wee San (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I believe that this would help many small to medium-sized arts groups, such as the Siong Leng Musical Association, Nam Hwa Opera and Singapore Traditional Arts Centre, so that they can benefit from CMF despite limited fundraising resources.

sections.label: Structural challenges and COVID-19
sections.summary: Singapore has faced structural challenges including an ageing population, rising social spending and falling revenues, with COVID-19 adding economic harm this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Singapore has, for many years, faced structural challenges that each Budget has had to address, including an ageing population, ever-increasing demands for social spending, particularly in healthcare, and a risk of falling revenues as the workforce shrinks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This year, we had an added spanner thrown into the works with the COVID-19 virus threatening lives, but which has also had a withering impact on our economy.

sections.label: Rental and wage support
sections.summary: Rental and property tax rebates send a message the Government is buffering pain, and the Wage Support Scheme cushions employers from wage costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Rental is a big concern for many businesses, and the provision of rental rebates as well as property tax rebates to property owners sends a strong message that the Government is helping to buffer some of this pain.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Wage Support Scheme helps to cushion employers from wage costs, and I hope they take the message to try and keep their employees for as long as possible.

sections.label: Confirmed cases still in hospital
sections.summary: Of 33 confirmed cases still in hospital, most are stable or improving, though seven remain critical in intensive care.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Of the 33 confirmed cases who are still in hospital, most are stable or improving although seven remain in critical condition and in intensive care.

sections.label: China virus economic impact
sections.summary: China's economy was hit hard, its growth forecast revised down to 4.5%, and the impact could affect Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: China’s economy has already been hit hard by the virus, with its growth forecast revised down to 4.5% in the last quarter, the lowest since the Global Financial Crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If this becomes a global pandemic and different countries take different measures, the economic impact could have longer-term implications for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: As it is, the drop in business from China has hurt our economy and many others in the world as China is the world’s second largest economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If large numbers of businesses fail or close during this period, the implications on growth could be significant and Singapore will not be cushioned.

sections.label: Retraining for workers losing jobs
sections.summary: Workers who may lose their jobs are urged to use measures including SkillsFuture top-ups to retrain and pick up new skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For workers who may lose their job during this period, please understand it is a difficult economy, but please make use of the wide range of measures available, including the SkillsFuture top-ups, to retrain and try and pick up new skills.

sections.label: Accumulated Budget surplus
sections.summary: Over the current term of Government, this House has accumulated a Budget surplus of over $17.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Over the current term of Government, this House has accumulated a Budget surplus of over $17.4 billion.

sections.label: GST timing and tax rebate
sections.summary: A Member asks when the eventual GST hike will be implemented, noting GST stays at 7% for 2021 and a 25% Corporate Income Tax Rebate for 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Ultimately, Sir, they not only had to work longer hours, but literally put their lives on the line.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: I am keenly aware of the Government’s announcement that GST will remain at 7% for 2021 and the $6 billion Assurance Package for Singaporeans to cushion the projected increase in GST.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: While I understand that we cannot put off the increase indefinitely, can the Minister give an indication of when the eventual hike will be implemented?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Lastly, turning away from GST, I also note that the Deputy Prime Minister has announced a Corporate Income Tax Rebate of 25% for 2020.

sections.label: Startup SG Equity agrifood startups
sections.summary: The Budget commits to setting aside a portion of the $300 million under Startup SG Equity for agrifood-related deep-tech startups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: The Budget commits to setting aside a portion of the $300 million under the Startup SG Equity in supporting agrifood-related deep-tech startups.

sections.label: Natural gas electricity and EVs
sections.summary: 95% of electricity comes from natural gas, raising the question of incentivising EVs without cleaner generation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: First, 95% of our electricity is generated from natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Insofar as we do not transition toward cleaner sources of electricity generation, what will be the impact of incentivising EVs be?

sections.label: SkillsFuture and workers over 60
sections.summary: Asks how to incentivise more worker upgrading and whether SkillsFuture top-ups can extend to those over 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Although we have done well to promote the ethos of lifelong learning in Singapore and with Singaporeans' take-up rate of SkillsFuture being at 49% in 2019, how can we incentivise more of our workers to upgrade themselves?

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Second, and related to the first point, I am concerned that the current SkillsFuture programme does not maximise the potential of all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: I note that Budget 2020 does not provide any SkillsFuture top-ups for workers aged over 60.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: Given our increasing longevity, I wonder if the hon Minister can extend the additional top-up to those aged over 60?

sections.label: Locally Trained and Globally Framed
sections.summary: Calls for cross-cultural skills and international understanding, citing Budget 2020's 70-70 exposure target and Australia's New Colombo Plan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: This is where the phrase "Locally Trained and Globally Framed" comes in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: We need to ensure that our students acquire the cross-cultural skills and deep international understanding which would enable them to compete with the best in the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: I am heartened that Budget 2020 sets a target for 70-70 exposure in our IHL students.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: In this regard, the New Colombo Plan initiative by the Australian Government is a model worth studying.

sections.label: Budget 2020 stability and investment
sections.summary: Budget 2020 provides stability while long-term investments in infrastructure and people are needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: In this time of crisis, Budget 2020 provides some much-needed stability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad
sentences.text: However, we must always look towards the future by making long-term investments in our infrastructure and our people to ensure Singapore is staged for success.

sections.label: GDP, productivity and indebtedness
sections.summary: Notes low 2019 GDP growth, bifurcated productivity, and possible chronic indebtedness for micro businesses from the coronavirus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In 2019, however, our GDP growth was low against even developed Asian economies like Korea, Taiwan and Australia, let alone the US, and this was before the coronavirus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Second, our productivity performance goes up and down, but it is also bifurcated between high productivity, manufacturing and other externally oriented sectors and some less productive sectors, and between a multinational corporation (MNC) sector with higher productivity and an SME sector that employs two-thirds of our workers with less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In fact, it is argued in a recent letter in the media from the Chairman of Credit Counselling Singapore, many micro businesses may become ensnared in a cycle of chronic indebtedness as a result of the economic impact from the coronavirus episode, as happened with SARS in 2003.

sections.label: Young Singaporeans considering migration
sections.summary: A recent survey found 29% of young Singaporeans would consider migrating in the next five years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Twenty-nine percent of young Singaporeans in a recent survey said that they would consider migrating in the next five years.

sections.label: Adjusting Silver Support for inflation
sections.summary: Silver Support could be adjusted for inflation by policy design rather than left to Government and Parliament's discretion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: One example of this would be adjusting Silver Support for inflation from time to time based on policy design rather than leaving it to the Government and Parliament at its discretion.

sections.label: Large Reserves and Net Investment Returns
sections.summary: Large Reserves yield Net Investment Returns, the largest state revenue stream today, drawable in emergencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: To be sure, it is a good thing that we have large Reserves that yield Net Investment Returns (NIR), the largest state revenue stream today and that can be drawn down in emergencies.

sections.label: How Reserves grow yearly
sections.summary: Reserves grow each year from half the NIR, land sales and unspent surplus from each term of government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Every year, these Reserves grow from half of the NIR as well as from land sales and any unspent surplus from each term of government, among other things.

sections.label: Drawdown during 2008 Global Financial Crisis
sections.summary: During the 2008 Global Financial Crisis, only a tiny fraction of the Reserves was drawn down.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Let us bear in mind that during the worst global economic crisis the world had ever seen since the Great Depression of the 1930s, during the Global Financial Crisis of 2008, we drew down only a tiny fraction of the Reserves.

sections.label: Korea's chaebol loan support policy
sections.summary: Korea in the 1960s and 1970s insured loans to chaebols that grew exports, withdrawing support from those that did not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: And why not let the winners pick themselves?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This was the philosophy of Korea in the 1960s and 1970s, where the state insured provision of loans to chaebols or large firms, which could consistently grow exports and hard currency earnings and loan support was withdrawn from those that could not consistently deliver those results.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: While to be sure that not everything Korea did in those decades was correct in hindsight, that policy contributed to the emergence of giant companies like Samsung and LG today.

sections.label: Mentoring civil servants becoming entrepreneurs
sections.summary: A 2018 Parliamentary answer said 26% of autonomous university graduates enter the Public Service as their first job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Twenty-six percent of autonomous university graduates go into the Public Service as their first job, according to a Parliamentary answer given in 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Can we create a programme that mentors and coaches civil servants in their 30s, 40s or 50s who wish to leave the service to become entrepreneurs?

sections.label: Jobs at risk from Industry 4.0
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a project can map jobs at risk from Industry 4.0 and inform workers to reskill into high-growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fourthly, can we undertake a project to map out the categories of jobs at risk from Industry 4.0 and then initiate a programme to inform workers in these sectors of the imminent risks over the mid and long term and nudge them to engage in reskilling and career switches to high-growth disruptive industries?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Perhaps an incentive scheme could be deployed to attract local workers into Industry 4.0 sectors, like renewable energy, drones, AI and deep tech, especially those sectors where the Singaporean Core is weak.

sections.label: Tracking people's capacities internationally
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether independent measures can regularly track Singaporeans' capacities, such as resilience, entrepreneurship and creativity, against other countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, as part of the Singapore Public Sector Outcomes Review (SPOR), can we adopt independent measures that regularly track the capacities of our people versus other countries in terms of attributes, like resilience, entrepreneurship and creativity?

sections.label: Financial Planning Attitudes Survey findings

sentences.text: And just 20% of those surveyed felt the need to do financial planning only when they are looking at retirement.

sections.label: Shrinking family sizes

sections.label: Younger generation's overseas exposure and gig work

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, an increasing proportion of our younger generation are gaining overseas exposures at study or work, and some are involved in the gig economy.

sections.label: Support for people with special needs

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: While some would argue that many recognise the need to include people with special needs and acknowledge their existence, I cannot agree that we have truly taken actions to be more inclusive in embracing people with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: There seems to be a lack of in-depth lifecycle planning support pillars for people with special needs from childhood to adulthood to their old age.

sections.label: Affordable legal support and assistance schemes

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: Second, provision of affordable legal support and streamline the search process of assistance schemes suitable for their needs.

sections.label: Guiding principle for extending support

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: This continues to be the guiding principle in our process of extending financial and broad-based support to the society.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
sentences.text: But as we progress in our nation-building, it is also our responsibility to deliberate how much more we can do, whether a fiscally sustainable assessment is made for support packages and how do we address the future state of support that we hope it to be.

sections.label: Harvard and WHO praise Singapore

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: A Harvard study described Singapore as having "gold standard" for case detection; WHO was "very impressed" by Singapore’s response to COVID-19.

sections.label: Stabilisation and Support Package for companies

sentences.text: The $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package helps companies to stay liquid, thus preserving the jobs of Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In particular, SMEs – comprising 72% of our employment – are most in need of supportive measures to help them retain local employees.

sections.label: Member companies offer low interest loans

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I was told that the responses from SMEs have been overwhelmingly positive.

sections.label: Extending working capital loan to freelancers

sentences.text: Could the Government consider extending the working capital loan to this group of freelance workers?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Or help them access the other measures aimed at helping businesses with cash flow to keep them afloat as well?

sections.label: McKinsey global manpower gaps survey
sections.summary: A February 2020 McKinsey article reported 87% of surveyed companies worldwide face or expect manpower gaps within a few years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In a February 2020 McKinsey article, it was reported that 87% of companies surveyed around the world say they either are experiencing manpower gaps now or expect to experience it within a few years.

sections.label: Global reskilling by 2030

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One billion people globally need to be reskilled by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, the Asia Ready Exposure Programme, together with the Global Ready Talent Programme, are timely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Business China, too, is working closely with MOE and other agencies to promote internship opportunities for our tertiary students and young working adults to intern in China, and the response was encouraging.

sections.label: Singapore AI blockchain window
sections.summary: Some corporate big wigs believe Singapore may have only a one-to-two-year window to get ahead in AI and blockchain technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: In view of the shortage of talent around the world, some corporate big wigs believe that Singapore may only have a window of opportunity of one to two years to get ahead in AI and blockchain technology.

sections.label: Coding curriculum and lifelong learning
sections.summary: The passage proposes incorporating coding into mainstream curriculum and instilling lifelong learning, encouraging use of SkillsFuture Credit for future-economy courses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: One, incorporate coding into mainstream curriculum, ensure that all Singaporean children have a basic understanding of coding so that they can have a headstart.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Two, instil the spirit of lifelong learning in our people and encourage them to make use of the SkillsFuture Credit to take up courses relevant to the future economy.

sections.label: Budget 2020 support measures
sections.summary: Budget 2020 includes Care and Nurture and Stabilise and Support Packages, with grocery, GST, kindergarten, transport and school meal subsidies helping lower-income families.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Budget 2020 is no exception, especially with its Care and Nurture and Stabilise and Support Packages.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome the various measures, including grocery and GST Vouchers, kindergarten, transport and school meal subsidies, that will certainly help lower-income families ease their financial burdens.

sections.label: Mentorship for less advantaged children
sections.summary: The passage calls for more systematic mentorship so children from less advantaged backgrounds are inspired by role models who rose from similar circumstances.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To more directly address such discouraging perceptions, we need to initiate more systematic mentorship for children of less advantaged backgrounds so that they are inspired by role models who have successfully risen from similar circumstances.

sections.label: Progressive data-sharing mandate regulation
sections.summary: A professor suggests a progressive data-sharing mandate forcing large companies to share data with smaller competitors, and Singapore should consider pioneering such regulation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Oxford University professor Viktor Mayer-Schönberger, co-author of Reinventing Capitalism in the Age of Big Data, suggests adopting a “progressive data-sharing mandate” that forces companies above a certain size to share some of their data with smaller competitors.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Just as Singapore was a frontrunner as one of the first countries to launch a Model AI Governance framework, we should also consider blazing the trail and pioneer regulation on the collection and use of big data.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-ups Budget 2020
sections.summary: The passage applauds the SkillsFuture Credit top-ups in Budget 2020 because a transforming economy requires a prepared workforce.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Precisely because our economy is maturing and transforming, change is, indeed, the only constant, and our workforce has to be prepared for that reality.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I, therefore, applaud the SkillsFuture Credit top-ups in Budget 2020.

sections.label: Jobs Support Scheme wage offset package
sections.summary: A $4 billion package offsets wages for three months to help an estimated 1.9 million local workers through the Jobs Support Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The $4 billion package announced to help workers remain employed through three months of offset wages offer a vital lifeline in current climes.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By helping an estimated 1.9 million local workers through this key Jobs Support Scheme, we can help to allay the anxieties of these workers and their families and demonstrate that ours is an inclusive society where we have a head but also a heart.

sections.label: SGX relaxed quarterly reporting
sections.summary: After a Parliamentary Question in January 2020, SGX relaxed quarterly reporting and announced half-yearly reporting will suffice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Following my Parliamentary Question in January 2020, last month, I am glad that SGX has relaxed the need for quarterly reporting and announced that half-yearly reporting will suffice.

sections.label: Singapore firms listed in Hong Kong

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2019, 10 Singapore firms were listed in Hong Kong, raising US$155 million.

sentences.text: The number of companies registered on SGX fell to 741 at the end of 2018, from a peak of 782 in 2010.

sections.label: EV incentives and road tax
sections.summary: The speaker supports Singapore's green transport drive and notes the EV Early Adoption Incentive and additional road tax for EVs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Thus, we are fully supportive of Singapore’s drive to move towards a sustainable and "green" transport and phase out petrol and diesel vehicles by 2040.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am heartened by MOF’s announcement to launch an EV Early Adoption Incentive (EEAI) by providing 45% rebate off the Additional Registration Fees (ARF), capped at $20,000 and subject to a minimum ARF of $5,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: At the same time, the Government will impose an additional road tax of up to $700 per year for EVs.

sections.label: Hydrogen vehicle feasibility study
sections.summary: China, Japan and South Korea are working on hydrogen vehicles, and the PMO awarded a hydrogen feasibility study to Kellogg Brown and Root.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: China, Japan and South Korea are already working to put millions of hydrogen-powered vehicles on their roads, because it is not only cleaner, its driving range and refuelling time are comparable to gasoline cars.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: We understand that in the second half of 2019, that is, last year, the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) awarded a hydrogen feasibility study to American engineering giant Kellogg Brown and Root, to assess the feasibility of importing hydrogen for downstream uses, ranging from vehicle fuelling to power generation.

sections.label: Taxi driver rental rebates
sections.summary: Taxi drivers will receive $10 per day from the Government, $10 per day from taxi companies, and another $16.50 in daily rebates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Taxi drivers will receive a rental rebate of $10 per day from the Government, and another $10 per day in rental rebates from taxi companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Taxi companies then decided to provide another $16.50 in daily rental rebates to taxi drivers.

sections.label: Additional taxi rental rebates
sections.summary: Some taxi companies including ComfortDelGro Taxi provide additional rebates, giving cabbies up to $36.50 per day until end-March 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Some taxi companies, including ComfortDelGro Taxi, is providing additional rental rebate of up to $26.50 over and above the SRF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: That is, cabbies are getting a total rental rebate of up to $36.50 per day until the end of March 2020.

sections.label: Freelancer cancellation fee appeal
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to MOF to let Government agencies pay up to 50% of freelancers' fees when engagements are cancelled due to COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (Jurong)
sentences.text: For such cases, I would like to appeal to MOF to allow the Government agencies to pay up to 50% of the fees charged by freelancers even when their engagements are cancelled due to COVID-19.

sections.label: Statute of Labourers 1351
sections.summary: The 1351 Statute of Labourers banned wages above pre-Plague levels and appears to have contributed to the 1381 peasant revolt.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In England, the Statute of Labourers 1351 made it illegal for workers to demand pay greater than those wages prevailing before the Plague.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While there is little evidence it was effective, it appears to have contributed to a major English peasant revolt in 1381.

sections.label: Chinese tourists and Budget 2020
sections.summary: In 2018, 3.4 million tourist arrivals were from China, Singapore's largest trading partner, and the speaker supports Budget 2020's intent.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In 2018, 3.4 million tourist arrivals – nearly one in five that year – were from China, and China is our largest trading partner.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The efforts of Budget 2020 to address the economic impact of COVID-19, and beyond that, to restructure the economy, are timely and I fully support the intent behind them.

sections.label: Market prices versus social value
sections.summary: The crisis has highlighted a growing divergence between market prices and social value.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The key contradiction which the present crisis has highlighted is the growing and invidious divergence between market prices and social value.

sections.label: Concentrated PPE production

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Market forces have concentrated the production of medical personal protective equipment, such as surgical masks, in a relatively small number of factories worldwide, many of them in China.

sections.label: Efficiency as sole criterion

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The COVID-19 outbreak, however, demonstrates the limitations of efficiency as the sole judgement criterion.

sections.label: Private specialists and public hospitals
sections.summary: Private specialist care gives patients choice and makes Singapore a medical hub, but a worsening outbreak may stretch GPs and public hospitals while private specialists lack work.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It gives patients choice; it makes Singapore a medical hub.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But it is likely, if the COVID-19 outbreak worsens, that our GPs and public hospitals will continue to be severely stretched with a high caseload while the private specialist sector may well be short of work.

sections.label: MOF income growth inequality paper
sections.summary: An MOF 2015 paper documents that from 2004 to 2009 cumulative per-member household income growth was 4% for the lowest quintile and 19.5% for the top quintile.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The occasional paper on "Income Growth, Inequality and Mobility Trends in Singapore" published by MOF in 2015, documents that from 2004 to 2009, cumulative per-member household income growth was only 4% for the the lowest quintile, as opposed to 19.5% for the top quintile.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Model and income growth

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the Government did not agree with Prof Lim's approach to the problem, it nonetheless worked through the tripartite framework to introduce the Progressive Wage Model, which provides an explicit framework for pushing salaries up in key low-wage sectors.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As reported in the latest Key Household Income Trends 2019, cumulative real growth in per-household member income was 29.5% and 31.8%, for the first and second deciles, from 2009 to 2019.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)

sections.label: Paying low-wage workers better

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The solution is to pay and respect low-wage workers better.

sections.label: Tangible salary increase for workers
sections.summary: It asks whether low-wage workers can be given a tangible salary increase to acknowledge their sacrifices, and says at least let us have the dollars.

sentences.text: Can we give them a tangible increase in their salaries to acknowledge their sacrifices?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we do not have the words to express our gratitude, then at least, let us have the dollars.

sections.label: CDC local assistance schemes

sentences.text: For example, in 2019, the CDCs rolled out 111 local assistance schemes that benefited close to 156,000 beneficiaries.

sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat has, in this year’s Budget, provided $20 million for the CDCs to better meet the needs of their residents through local initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: The $20 million Meals in the Heartlands initiative is expected to benefit some 100,000 vulnerable families and each CDC will administer the scheme accordingly to meet the needs of its residents.

sections.label: SMEs share of enterprises and employees
sections.summary: SMEs make up 99% of enterprises and hire close to 70% of employees in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: SMEs make up 99% of our enterprises and SMEs hire close to 70% of employees in Singapore.

sentences.text: Last year, 6,800 SMEs benefited from the business advisory sessions from the SME@CDC centres and another 2,400 companies took part in 60 capability workshops to enhance their brand, productivity and marketing.

sections.summary: SkillsFuture Advice started in 2017; by 2019 over 100,000 Singaporeans joined over 3,700 SkillsFuture Workshops in the heartlands.

sentences.text: In 2017, we started SkillsFuture Advice to help Singaporeans navigate their lifelong learning journey and capture opportunities to skill up with courses that they can attend with their SkillsFuture Credits.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: By 2019, more than 100,000 Singaporeans have participated in over 3,700 SkillsFuture Workshops in the heartlands, in the community.

sections.label: Funding for Care and ComCare
sections.summary: Besides the $1.6 billion Care and Support Package, the Government will set aside $20 million for ComCare schemes under the CDCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In terms of funding, besides the $1.6-billion-dollar Care and Support Package, the Government will also set aside $20 million for ComCare schemes under the CDCs.

sections.label: 2019 measures and advisory service use

sentences.text: In 2019, we implemented 111 measures that helped more than 150,000 beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Manpower (Ms Low Yen Ling)
sentences.text: In 2019, about 6,800 shops have made use of this advisory service.

sections.label: Stimulus packages and tax rebate
sections.summary: The speaker supports stimulus, citing $4 billion Stabilisation and Support Package, $8.3 billion Transformation and Growth Strategy, and a 25% Corporate Income Tax rebate capped at $15,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This is why I support the Government’s efforts to inject additional stimulus in the economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I am especially appreciative of the Stabilisation and Support Package where $4 billion will be made available to local businesses to tide over short-term dislocations, and the Transformation and Growth Strategy where $8.3 billion will be made available to local businesses to position for the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Stabilisation and Support Package will help small enterprises but it is really too small for medium enterprises.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The Corporate Income Tax rebate of 25% of tax payable is a welcome measure, but it is capped at $15,000.

sections.label: Bank loan approval timing
sections.summary: Banks say new loan approvals take until mid-March and disbursement until mid-April.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: From what I heard from the banks, it will take until mid-March to approve new loans and these loans will not be disbursed until mid-April.

sections.label: Training, jobs and local talent

sentences.text: They need the training to get a job, but need to get the job to get the training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I would urge the Government to provide more than the hiring incentive of 20% salary, capped at six months that is announced in the Budget, in order to further incentivise companies to make the first move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Similarly, in the area of manpower, we need to build up our self-sufficiency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: I would encourage the Government to identify areas of critical need or essential services, and to build up a core of local talent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It might be cheaper to outsource in the short term, but the strategic value of insourcing would be very apparent and outweigh the cost when disaster hits.

sections.label: Mittelstand fund for SMEs

sentences.text: Would he consider extending the support package to more sectors?
