sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For example, being upfront with Singaporeans early about the future hike in GST, being open about why over reliance on the NIRC may not be fiscally prudent and why, at this stage, we need to think of raising GST in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If I may be bold enough to say, it is the same framework that we see being deployed within the COVID-19 task force – sharing the infection numbers, the discharged numbers, the intensive care unit (ICU) numbers, sharing information about the clusters and, importantly, readying Singaporeans for the method we will use to deal with the virus in the longer time, whichever of the scenarios plays out.

sections.label: Hierarchical views of jobs and professions
sections.summary: The passage suggests using the COVID-19 outbreak to remove hierarchical views that treat some professions as more prestigious and other jobs as less dignified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Perhaps, in this moment of the COVID-19 outbreak, we should also take the opportunity to try to remove the hierarchical way that some in our society view jobs and professions, with certain professions viewed as more prestigious while other jobs are viewed as less dignified.

sections.label: Everyone important during COVID-19
sections.summary: The passage states that the COVID-19 crisis proves everyone is important, has a role to play and is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If anything, the COVID-19 crisis is proof to all of us that everyone is important, everyone has a role to play, everyone is needed.

sections.label: Restaurant survey and sector support
sections.summary: A Restaurant Association Singapore survey found close to 60% of restaurants unprepared for COVID-19, with tourist-reliant ones facing up to 80% losses, and the passage notes expanded Adapt and Grow and rental waivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: According to a snap survey done by Restaurant Association Singapore, close to 60% of restaurants in Singapore stated that they are not prepared and equipped enough to deal with the impact of COVID-19 on their operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For those who rely heavily on tourists, the estimated loss could go up to 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To help the food and services sector during this period, the Adapt and Grow initiative was expanded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In relation to rental costs, for F&B and retailers, it is good that there are full month rental waivers for some hawkers and half a month of rental waivers for commercial tenants of Government agencies.

sections.label: SMU core curriculum and lifelong learning
sections.summary: The passage states SMU's core curriculum was designed to nurture adaptive, adroit graduates and instils an aptitude for and attitude of lifelong learning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: SMU's core curriculum was designed to nurture a generation of "adaptive and adroit graduates who are technically competent and agile, socially conscious and adept in their communities and inspired by the timeless puzzles and challenges confronting humanity." This instills in students the aptitude for and attitude of lifelong learning.

sections.label: Singapore Strait sea level rise
sections.summary: Data from four sites show a 2.9-millimetre yearly sea level increase from 1984 to 2011, threatening low-lying nations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Historical data measuring average sea levels of the Singapore Strait from four research-quality data points at Tanjong Pagar, Raffles Lighthouse, Sultan Shoal and Sembawang, indicate that there was a 2.9-millimetre yearly increase of our sea levels from 1984 to 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What this means is that low-lying small nations, such as the Maldives and Tuvalu may face, or, in fact, are facing existential crisis.

sections.label: Budget sea level investment
sections.summary: The Budget's $5 billion investment to address rising sea levels' effects on Singapore is called commendable and far-sighted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Because of the dire consequences rising sea levels have on Singapore's future, it is good that the Budget takes these longer-term challenges into account and prepares for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The $5 billion investment to ameliorate the effect that sea levels have on Singapore is thus commendable and far-sighted.

sections.label: Budget debate and unity
sections.summary: The Budget Statement and its debate focus on getting through the storm as one united people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: The Budget Statement and the debate on it are important to train our focus on how to ensure we get through the storm as one united people.

sections.label: Resilience of public servants
sections.summary: Reserves of strength, resilience, empathy and resourcefulness among public servants and Singaporeans allow planning well beyond this storm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: I also mean the reserves of	strength,	resilience,	empathy and resourcefulness among our public servants and fellow Singaporeans".

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: It is such resilience that allows us to plan well into the future, well beyond this storm.

sections.label: Budget titles emphasise unity
sections.summary: From 2016, all Budget titles emphasised unity, ending this year with advancing as one Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From 2016, all the titles of each Budget emphasised "unity" – partnering for the future, moving forward together, together a better future, building a strong and united Singapore, and finally, this year, advancing as one Singapore.

sections.label: Chambers acknowledge support package
sections.summary: Discussions with local Chambers of Commerce members showed general acknowledgement of relief from the Budget's Stabilisation and Support Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: My brief discussions, after the Budget was announced, with a few members of the various local Chambers of Commerce informed me that there has been a general acknowledgement of the relief provided by the Stabilisation and Support Package in the Budget.

sections.label: Private bus companies Budget support
sections.summary: Private bus companies feel the Budget support package is not targeted enough given their business nature.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While the briefing was appreciated, private bus companies feel the Budget support package is not targeted enough, in view of the nature of their business.

sections.label: NIRC, GST offsets, COVID-19 funding
sections.summary: Temasek's inclusion in NIRC from 2016 allows GST offset monies to be set aside for higher taxes; COVID-19 support was not funded from Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: After the inclusion of Temasek in the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) component of the Budget from 2016, monies for the GST offset package can be set aside for the introduction of higher taxes for the next term of Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Separately, the package to support the economy in light of COVID-19 was not funded from a draw on the Reserves, unlike the support package during the Global Financial Crisis about a decade ago.

sections.label: Borrowing for long-term infrastructure
sections.summary: The Finance Minister raised Statutory Board and Government-owned company borrowing for infrastructure in 2018 and 2019 speeches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: More specifically, in the Finance Minister's 2018 speech, the prospect of borrowing by Statutory Boards and Government-owned companies to build infrastructure was first raised to help spread the cost of larger investments over many years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This prospect of borrowing was raised again by the Finance Minister in his 2019 Budget speech where the Finance Minister confirmed that the Government is studying the option of using Government debt as part of the financing mix for long-term infrastructure projects.

sections.label: GST regressive tax impact
sections.summary: Despite offsets, GST is regressive and will hit low- and middle-income, retirees and seniors hard as offsets do not last forever.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding the offsets announced, the GST is a regressive tax that will hit the low- and middle-income, retirees and seniors particularly hard as they would have to manage their expenditures more frugally because offsets do not last forever, particularly for the middle-class.

sections.label: WP cannot support GST hike
sections.summary: The WP's position has not changed and it cannot support a GST hike raised in advance before projections are put to the House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Until this clarity is provided, the WP's position has not changed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We cannot support a GST hike, especially since this is to be raised in advance and before the Government's projections have been put to this House.

sections.label: Reviewing courses for workers
sections.summary: An audit of courses taken by younger- and middle-aged Singaporeans must be reviewed with ITM stakeholders for best medium-term outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: An audit of the courses our people are taking up, particularly younger- and middle-aged Singaporeans, must be reviewed every so often in consultation with inputs from the Industry Transformation Map (ITM) stakeholders, so as to evince the best outcomes possible for our workers in the medium term.

sections.label: Transitional subsidy for plastic bags
sections.summary: A $20 transitional subsidy for households to buy plastic bags at supermarkets could bridge Singaporeans before a per-bag charge by all retailers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For example, a transitional subsidy amounting to $20 for households to subsidise the purchase of plastic bags at supermarkets could be considered as a bridge for Singaporeans before a charge is levied for every bag by all retailers.

sections.label: Waste reduction and Semakau space
sections.summary: The passage calls for changing social norms to reduce waste, citing limited space on Pulau Semakau expected to be full by 2035 and 342,304 MEWR pledges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It is a clarion call to us all to alter our social norms to equally, if not more importantly, reduce the amount of waste we generate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This is a pressing issue as there are infrastructural constraints on the amount of space we have to dispose of our incinerated waste on Pulau Semakau which is expected to be full by 2035 or thereabouts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Correct as of Monday, there were 342,304 pledges on the MEWR website to fight climate change.

sections.label: Estimated deficit of $10.95 billion
sections.summary: The passage states that the estimated position is a deficit of $10.95 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Overall, we estimate our position to be in deficit of $10.95 billion.

sections.label: 2020 Budget deficit and no Reserve draw
sections.summary: The 2020 Budget deficit funds COVID-19 measures including $4 billion Stabilisation and Support and $1.6 billion Care and Support packages, with no draw on Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: A large part of the estimated Budget deficit for 2020, as Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat has explained in his Budget Statement, it should fund measures to address the impending difficult economic landscape that confronts Singapore as a result of the COVID-19 virus outbreak.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: This includes the $4 billion Stabilisation and Support package for workers and businesses and also the $1.6 billion Care and Support package to help Singaporeans with household expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In the Budget Statement, the sentence that captured my attention the most was when Deputy Prime Minister Heng announced that there will be no draw on our Reserves; no draw on our Reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: For financial year (FY) 2020, we have an expansionary Budget with an estimated $10.5 billion deficit, but we need not draw on our Reserves.

sections.label: Building a profitable consumer product business
sections.summary: The speaker hid which companies he owned, worked behind the scenes, built his business layer by layer, and his consumer product venture is now profitable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: On the other hand, I took a lot of measures and also a lot of different ways to hide and not show which companies I owned and how I did it and actually worked behind the scenes really, really hard in order to grow those businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: So, piece by piece, layer by layer, I built my business and I am very lucky, very blessed that, today, my venture in the consumer product business is profitable.

sections.label: Temporary relief and building Reserves
sections.summary: The passage says relief measures are temporary, someone must want to buy your product to invest, and slowing Reserves growth is not the way to go.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Yes, they are temporary relief measures, but they are not permanent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: At the end of the day, someone must want to buy your product, work with you and believe in your company in order to invest in it in order for it to grow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But I think slowing down the growth of the Reserves is not the way to go because, no matter what, we need to build up the foundation in order to take on the rainy days or challenges to come and deal with COVID-19.

sections.label: Grants risk business welfare state
sections.summary: The speaker says business schemes are increasingly targeted, but too many grants and schemes risk creating a welfare state for businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I think more and more of those schemes for businesses are now very targeted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But having too many of those grants and schemes and we risk going into a welfare state for businesses.

sections.label: Schemes for government bank loan risk
sections.summary: The speaker says that if something cannot be done, there are schemes where the Government takes up a greater risk of the bank loan.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: If we cannot, well, there are schemes where the Government is taking up a greater risk of the bank loan.

sections.label: NTUC Job Security Council matching PMEs
sections.summary: The speaker says NTUC came up with the Job Security Council and suggests accessing its PMEs to see where matching can be done.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: NTUC actually came up with the Job Security Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Maybe it is something that we can have access to some of the professionals, managers and executives (PMEs) over there to see where we can do the matching.

sections.label: Newer markets to expand revenue base
sections.summary: The speaker describes finding a market that used to cost 30% higher and now costs 30% lower to launch a product, offering an opportunity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: But where are the newer markets to expand your market and expand your revenue base?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Ser Luck (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: And we realised that one of the markets that we are going to used to be 30% higher cost and is now 30% lower cost if I were to launch my product there and I thought "Why not?" That offers an opportunity.

sections.label: Care and Support Packages
sections.summary: The speaker says that in challenging times they acted decisively to protect families and workers through the Care and Support Package and the Stabilisation and Support Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In these challenging times, we have acted decisively to protect families and workers through the Care and Support Package and the Stabilisation and Support Package.

sections.label: Budget 2020 spending size
sections.summary: The speaker says Budget 2020 spending is appropriate for now, calibrated to put purchasing power into the economy and boost confidence, and is higher than most economists expected.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The overall size of our spending in Budget 2020 is appropriate for now.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have calibrated it to put sufficient purchasing power back into the economy, while injecting a boost of confidence.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In fact, our Budget is higher than what most economists had expected.

sections.label: SME payouts as revenue percentage
sections.summary: SMEs will receive payouts that, as a percentage of revenue, average five times the average for all enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As a percentage of revenue, SMEs will receive payouts that are, on average, five times as much as the average for all enterprises.

sections.label: Sector support over $400 million
sections.summary: These sectors will receive over $400 million in total, in addition to broad-based support from JSS, WCS and Corporate Income Tax Rebate.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In total, these sectors will receive over $400 million, in addition to the broad-based support that they will get through JSS, WCS and Corporate Income Tax Rebate.

sections.label: Support for drivers, hawkers, guides, outlets
sections.summary: Additional measures support taxi and private hire car drivers, hawkers, tourist guides and food and beverage and retail outlet operators, totalling over $200 million.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have provided additional measures to support taxi and private hire car drivers, hawkers, tourist guides and operators of food and beverage and retail outlets.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This additional support totals over $200 million and is over and above the support from broad-based measures, which form the bulk of the support for them.

sections.label: JSS payment brought forward
sections.summary: Agencies have redoubled efforts and now target bringing forward the JSS payment from end-July to end-May.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the last few weeks, the agencies involved have redoubled efforts and are now targeting to bring forward the payment for JSS from end-July to end-May.

sections.label: SBF YBLN Hope Fund
sections.summary: Young leaders from six business families in the SBF YBLN set up a $5 million fund to provide financing help for local enterprises hit by COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Young leaders from six business families in the Singapore Business Federation Young Business Leaders Network (SBF YBLN), has set up a $5 million fund called the Helping Our Promising Enterprises (SBF YBLN) and Hope Fund to provide financing help for local enterprises hit by COVID-19.

sections.label: Bonuses, recognition and clinic grant
sections.summary: Frontline public officers battling COVID-19 will get up to one additional month of special bonus, other contributors recognised, and a one-off grant made to Public Health Preparedness Clinics.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Government will award public officers on the frontline who are directly battling with the COVID-19 disease up to one additional month of special bonus.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Other public officers who have contributed significantly will be recognised in appropriate ways.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We will also make a one-off COVID-19 grant to the Public Health Preparedness Clinics to support them in their active role caring for patients with respiratory symptoms.

sections.label: Political officeholders salary cut
sections.summary: All political officeholders will take a one-month salary cut to show solidarity with fellow Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To show solidarity with fellow Singaporeans, all political officeholders will take a one-month cut in their salary.

sections.label: GST increase and alternatives
sections.summary: The GST increase was announced for 2021 to 2025, and some suggested delaying or dropping it or raising other taxes instead.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Two years ago, I announced that we will need to raise the GST some time from 2021 to 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Some have called for the GST rate increase to be delayed or dropped completely after I announced that it would not take effect in 2021 and that we have prepared a $6 billion Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In place of the GST rate increases, some have suggested alternatives, including raising income and wealth taxes as well as spending our Reserves and more of its investment returns.

sections.label: Raising GST responsible way
sections.summary: The passage states raising GST remains the responsible way to meet society's future needs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: First, I will explain why raising GST remains the responsible way for all of us to meet our society's future needs.

sections.label: Healthcare spending and schemes
sections.summary: Government healthcare spending rose from about 0.7% of GDP in 2000 to about 2.1% in 2015, funding schemes like MediShield Life and CHAS.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In 2000, Government spending on healthcare was about 0.7% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By 2015, it had tripled to about 2.1% of our GDP.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This additional spending has gone towards significant improvements in healthcare accessibility and affordability.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have introduced new schemes, such as MediShield Life, and expanded the Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) to cover all Singaporeans for many chronic conditions.

sections.label: Citizens aged 80 and above
sections.summary: The number of citizens aged 80 and above almost doubled from 63,000 in 2009 to 112,000 in 2019 and will increase further.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The number of citizens aged 80 and above has almost doubled, from 63,000 in 2009 to 112,000 in 2019, and will increase further.

sections.label: Funding recurrent needs
sections.summary: Recurrent needs must be funded using recurrent revenues, not one-off surpluses from financial and property market rallies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: They are recurrent needs, meaning that these needs will be there year after year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, we need to fund them using recurrent revenues, not one-off surpluses seen in this term of Government, which arose from the unexpected rally in global financial markets and the unexpected buoyancy in the property market.

sections.label: Planning ahead to raise revenues
sections.summary: The outbreak reminds us why we need to plan ahead to raise revenues.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The outbreak reminds us why we need to plan ahead to raise revenues.

sections.label: Why GST for societal needs
sections.summary: Some who agree on raising taxes ask why GST, which is described as appropriate for paying for major societal needs like healthcare.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Yet, even among those who agree in principle on the need to raise taxes, some have asked, "Why GST?" As I have explained before, a broad-based tax like GST is an appropriate and responsible way to pay for major societal needs like healthcare spending.

sections.label: GST increase revenue share
sections.summary: A two percentage point GST increase will provide additional revenue of almost 0.7% of GDP per year.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: An increase of two percentage points in the GST rate will provide us with additional revenue of almost 0.7% of GDP per year.

sections.label: GST rate versus averages
sections.summary: After raising GST to 9%, it will still be lower than the average rate in Asia and less than half the OECD average.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: After raising the GST to 9%, it will still be lower than the average rate in Asia and less than half of the average rate in OECD countries today.

sections.label: Package delays GST impact
sections.summary: The package delays the GST increase impact for most Singaporean households for at least five years, and for lower-income Singaporeans for 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The package effectively delays the impact of the GST increase for the majority of Singaporean households for at least five years.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: For lower-income Singaporeans, the offset will be even higher and, hence, there is effectively no increase for them for 10 years.

sections.label: Who bears net GST
sections.summary: Foreigners residing in Singapore, tourists and the top 20% of resident households are estimated to account for over 60% of net GST borne.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Foreigners residing in Singapore, tourists and the top 20% of resident households are estimated to account for over 60% of the net GST borne by all households and individuals.

sections.label: GST increase delay support
sections.summary: The Assurance Package delays the GST increase for almost all Singaporeans by at least five years, and the permanent GST Voucher further helps lower- and middle-income people.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Through the Assurance Package, we will effectively delay the increase for almost all Singaporeans by at least five years; and over and above the transitional support, the permanent GST Voucher will further help the lower- and middle-income.

sections.label: NIRC FY2019 budget contribution
sections.summary: In FY2019, NIRC was $17 billion, or 3.3% of GDP, the largest single contributor to the Budget.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In FY2019, our NIRC was $17 billion, or 3.3% of GDP, the largest single contributor to the Budget.

sections.label: NIRC compared to taxes
sections.summary: NIRC at $17 billion exceeds personal income tax at $12 billion and GST at $11 billion, so doubling either would still not replace it.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, NIRC, at $17 billion, is more than personal income tax at $12 billion, and GST collections at $11 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, if we did not have NIRC, even doubling personal income tax, or doubling the GST rate to 14%, would still not be enough.

sections.label: Coastal and Flood Protection Fund
sections.summary: This Budget sets aside $5 billion for a Coastal and Flood Protection Fund for pumps, tidal gates and infrastructure against rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this Budget, I have set aside $5 billion for a Coastal and Flood Protection Fund.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I could have chosen instead to spend it on more "hong baos" or red packets to make myself more popular.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But by making the commitment today, these resources will go towards pumps, tidal gates and infrastructure that will keep our children and their children safe from rising sea levels in decades to come.

sections.label: Climate and food production plans
sections.summary: Agencies coordinated by the National Climate Change Secretariat will update the Paris Agreement commitment, submit a Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy, and MEWR pursues its 30 by 30 food production target.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Several agencies are working in concert to execute this, coordinated by the National Climate Change Secretariat.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year, we will update our commitment to the Paris Agreement and submit our Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy to contribute efforts to mitigate climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Just as it had done with water, MEWR is embarking on ambitious plans to develop our own food production capabilities with its "30 by 30" target.

sections.label: Glocalisation three things
sections.summary: Lim Swee Say's Glocalisation calls for transforming the economy to be globally competitive, developing people, and strengthening the social compact so no one is left behind.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Mr Lim Swee Say, in his trademark pithy way, said we need "Glocalisation" – both a globally competitive economy and a locally cohesive society.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This calls for us to do three things: to transform our economy to be globally competitive, to develop our people to seize these opportunities, and to strengthen our social compact by ensuring that all benefit from the fruits of progress and no one is left behind.

sections.label: Transforming Singapore's economy
sections.summary: Singapore began transforming its economy in 2016 with the Committee on the Future Economy, aiming to be a Global-Asia Node.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have, therefore, embarked on an urgent journey to transform Singapore's economy.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We started our work four years ago in 2016 when the Committee on the Future Economy was formed.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To ride on Asia’s growth, we are working to position Singapore as a Global-Asia Node of Technology, Innovation and Enterprise, as a trusted and valuable part of the network of global cities that are driving innovation and growth globally.

sections.label: Industry Transformation Maps partnership
sections.summary: Industries and enterprises are mobilised to own their transformation through Industry Transformation Maps across 23 sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Third, we are mobilising and partnering our industries and enterprises to take ownership of their own economic transformation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have brought industry stakeholders together via Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs) across 23 sectors.

sections.label: EDB 2019 investment commitments
sections.summary: The Economic Development Board attracted $15.2 billion in Fixed Asset Investments and $9 billion in Total Business Expenditure in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Investment commitments attracted by the Economic Development Board in 2019 amounted to $15.2 billion in Fixed Asset Investments and $9 billion in Total Business Expenditure per year.

sections.label: Local employment and income growth
sections.summary: Over 10 years local employment grew over 41,000 jobs yearly, unemployment stayed about 3.2%, and real incomes rose about 3% yearly.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Over the last 10 years, local employment has grown steadily, adding more than 41,000 jobs each year on average.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Local unemployment has stayed low, at about 3.2% of resident labour force in December 2019, on a seasonally-adjusted basis.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Since 2010, real incomes have risen by about 3% each year for the median full-time employed local worker.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package
sections.summary: This Budget introduced the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package, hiring incentives, and a $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up for Singaporeans aged 40 to 60.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In this Budget, we have built on these initiatives, paying special attention to the needs of mid-career workers in their 40s and 50s by introducing the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support Package.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are also increasing the capacity of our reskilling programmes by providing a hiring incentive to employers and providing a special SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500 to every Singaporean aged 40 to 60 in 2020.

sections.label: Next Bound of SkillsFuture
sections.summary: The Next Bound of SkillsFuture mobilises businesses to upskill workers and redesign jobs, with hiring incentives for those hiring local workers aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Next Bound of SkillsFuture announced in this Budget, therefore, mobilises businesses to upskill their workers and redesign jobs through the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit and the expansion of the Productivity Solutions Grant for job redesign consultancy services.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Enterprises which hire local workers aged 40 and above, with no upper age limit, through reskilling programmes will also get hiring incentives.

sections.label: Education subsidies per child
sections.summary: A Singaporean child receives over $180,000 in education subsidies, including preschool subsidies, by age 16.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In all, by the time a Singaporean child reaches 16, he or she would have received more than $180,000 in education subsidies, including preschool subsidies.

sections.label: Strengthening social compact
sections.summary: The third strategy is to strengthen the social compact so all benefit from the fruits of progress.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But for all our efforts to maximise opportunities for everyone, there will be some who will continue to face difficulties.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: So, our third strategy is to strengthen our social compact by ensuring that all benefit from the fruits of progress.

sections.label: Silver Support enhancements
sections.summary: Silver Support enhancements will benefit 100,000 more seniors and payouts are raised by 20%.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Second, there are retired seniors who had lower incomes in their working years, with little or no family support.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have announced substantial enhancements to Silver Support to benefit 100,000 more seniors and raised payouts by 20%.

sections.label: Budget help for families
sections.summary: This Budget gives families with young or school-going children extra cash payouts, more U-Save rebates and PAssion Card top-ups.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Financially, we have given additional help for such families in this Budget by providing those with young or school-going children with an extra $100 cash payout per parent, more GST Voucher – U-Save rebates for larger households and PAssion Card top-ups for their parents.

sections.label: Gini co-efficient after transfers
sections.summary: The Gini co-efficient after taxes and transfers fell to 0.398 last year, the lowest since 2001.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Gini co-efficient after taxes and transfers fell to 0.398 last year, the lowest since 2001.

sections.label: NIRC as largest revenue source
sections.summary: NIRC is the largest revenue source, exceeding corporate income tax, personal income tax or GST, and doubling GST would not suffice without it.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: NIRC is already the largest source of revenue for our country, more than the revenue collected from corporate income tax, personal income tax or GST.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Without NIRC, even doubling the GST rate to 14% would not be enough to meet our expenditures.

sections.label: GST rate and increase
sections.summary: Everyone bears some cost; GST stays at 7% in 2021 but Government must raise GST by 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is fair for everyone to bear some part of the cost.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I have announced that the GST rate will remain at 7% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: But the Government will still have to raise GST by 2025.

sections.label: GST support packages approach
sections.summary: Several packages form a multi-pronged approach to tackle immediate challenges and prepare Singaporeans and companies for economic recovery.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Assurance Package for GST, Stabilisation and Support Package, Care and Support Package and Transformation and Growth Strategy constitute the multi-pronged approach that ensures that Singapore does not lose sight of the direction that we are heading towards, as we tackle immediate challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: These measures will also allow Singaporeans and companies to prepare for the economic recovery during this period of economic slowdown.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We are able to do this because we have been prudent in managing our finances over the years, preparing for rainy days and setting aside sufficient funds.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: At the same time, we have been using our Reserves in a responsible manner.
